Top of the line room had issues. While the rooms have been updated recently, many features were either broken or run-down. The bathroom and walk-in closet doors wouldn't close properly, and the patio door didn't work, which limited our access to the outdoor space we were looking forward to. The steam iron did not work.  The AC system was also a problem—it wasn’t adjustable, maintaining a chilly 18°C at all times, which made the room uncomfortably cold, especially for families with kids.

Housekeeping was subpar, particularly at night. We requested that the sofa bed be made up for our child every night, but each time, we had to call repeatedly, and no one would show up for an hour or more. This lack of attention was frustrating and left us feeling neglected by the staff. Furthermore, the concierge service, which initially came across as helpful, turned out to be more focused on selling a timeshare-like membership than addressing any of our actual needs. It was clear that their friendliness was more about getting us into a presentation than providing genuine assistance.

Dining options were also limited and disappointing. More than half of the restaurants were closed most nights, restricting us to only a few places. The hostess at Flore restaurant was especially rude—she even skipped over us in line to serve people who arrived after us. This level of poor service is unacceptable, especially given the resort’s premium pricing. The buffet lacked variety, with the same vegetarian options repeated daily, and while the desserts were visually appealing, they all tasted the same. If you’re seeking flavorful cuisine, particularly Indian or Thai options, I’d recommend looking elsewhere.

A few positive notes: Miguel, a bartender at the restaurant, was fantastic. He was attentive and welcoming, standing out from the otherwise lackluster service. However, restaurant reservations were another hassle; they had to be made in advance, and though some restaurants appeared empty, they still wouldn’t take walk-ins. The main buffet was closed for dinner every night, which limited our options further.

Overall, this resort has declined significantly since our last visit. Unfortunately, with such deterioration in service, food quality, and room conditions, we wouldn’t choose to stay here again.

reviews.author: Arlo Hernandez
reviews.text: Resort is great, clean. Not crowded and having an Adult section certainly helps. Unfortunately, the fine-print when making a reservation at the restaurant onsite - max allowed time is 90min. The host will not sit you until your entire party arrives and are not flexible with any modifications- adding people to the reservation, knowing the establishment has plenty of empty tables. Bartenders are respectful, however the staff at the restaurants are not to par.

reviews.author: Tori Dittmann
reviews.text:
Currently sitting at the Italian restaurant, Mascalzone The food and service was great! Willamena, Bernabe and the supervisor Milton were very kind and accommodating!  The bread is really really wonderful 😂

Now for the rest of the trip:
Hotel rooms are nice, fridge stocked and snacks plentiful! Everything was super comfy and we liked the walk out garden patio. The walls are SO thin though. You can hear every word of the conversation happening next door. It’s really strange and every time they close the door, the adjoining door rattles so that’s a bummer.

Service everywhere is hit or miss. Loved the staff at the Ginger coffee bar and Kicks Sports Bar. Super nice and friendly. Victor, and the Miguels are the bartenders that stand out the most from Kicks - very attentive and nice! All the staff at Ginger Bar are fantastic and make great cups of coffee!

Service at Blue Agave was absolutely terrible and food was pretty mediocre. Flora was probably our favorite dinner, I dont remember her name, but our server was so sweet. Great atmosphere and service! Tokimeyku (Japanese food) was super fun and yummy as well, Kelvin and Raphael were hilarious! The Lunch Box for breakfast and lunch was good but lots of room for improvement. Yogurt and milk were never quite cold which was weird. Lots of food options but many dishes needed salt. Ice cream was super melty almost all the time.

Activities were… meh. Participated in a few things here and there but learned quickly they weren’t really worth it. Our concierge was very kind but difficult to get a hold of (used WhatsApp) and I had to ask almost every evening where our reservation was for the night. 2 nights our reservation was 9 or later which we had asked for early dinner on our first day here. The language barrier can also be a bit of a hindrance between all the bars, restaurants, housekeeping staff, etc because their English all varied.

We went to Bavaro Adventure Park for an excursion one day which was a blast! We booked it through the guys who sit in the lobby.

All in all, it was a great vacation but if I had to do it again, I’d probably try another resort just to see if there’s a difference. You also need to bring things to do (cards, books, water raft/activities, things like that) to occupy your time and plenty of sunscreen!

reviews.author: Kevin Lewis
reviews.text:
The food and service were major letdowns here.

The facility is beautiful with pools and gardens woven through with walkways. There are curves that join restaurants with the pool.

They could have used more ceiling fans throughout. The lobby area had some but would still get stifling hot in some areas. The reserve restaurant, Sante, had some in the circular area but none in the area closer to the buffet.

The rooms in the reserve were nice. The minibar was stocked every day with drinks and snacks. The "bathroom" area was large due to the use of a curtain instead of walls. The water closet was pretty small.

The food in the Flora restaurant was quite good. Everyone in our party enjoyed it.

Blue Agave was hit or miss, but once we found the right dishes, we were happy with it.

All the other restaurants were very disappointing. The worst being Mina, the steak house. The steaks were of poor quality and poorly prepared. But the sides were a disaster. The potatoes were closer to hockey pucks than anything edible. I am not joking.

The sports bar has beer on tap but the staff didn't know how much it cost and were confused if it was included in our reserve stay (it was). But even then they were out of most of the beers listed. It was truly a pitiful experience in the sports bar.

Throughout our stay the service was very poor. In the restaurants would disappear after seating us and never come back until they were waved down.

The reserve restaurant, Sante, was always painful. At breakfast, the servers are uninterested in anyone wanting to order of the menu. They want everyone to go to the buffet. And the buffet was not good.

The adults-only area continuously had a lot of children in the pool, at the bar, on the beach. And there are plenty of pools. There was no reason I could see that the children needed to be in the adult pool.

Overall, our stay was very disappointing. We would not go back.

reviews.author: P Lay
reviews.text:
I’m going to just start with a short description for those who don’t want to read the whole thing. I wouldn’t book again only because I know there are better resorts for the same price. Food and service was terrible but beach was great! If you want more details on why continue on reading.

Going to start with the pros: the room was nice and spacious, very beautiful. Got the king size bed so it was nice. The double room didn’t look as good. We stayed at the all adults sections. It was a little further walk to the main buffet, but not bad. The beach was nice and they did a good job of cleaning the seaweed in the am, so that the beach front was nice and enjoyable for the guest. The adult pool was good. Not too far from the airport, about a 25 min ride with a little bit of traffic, so not bad. They had a wrist band so you can get into your room with it, so no need to carry an extra key card, which was really convenient. The towels were abundant and didn’t need a towel card, bonus for that.

Cons: food was terrible, not many choices and the same thing was served at the buffet for most of the night. There was minimal things that was hard to get like mustard or dressing specifically ranch or Caesar and if you asked the staff did not know. Food was always overcooked on the grill, just dry hamburger, hotdogs, chicken, you name it… just dry all the time. We tried to make reservations for restaurant but it was hard to get into any as many were booked all the time. You can only make reservations in advance for the next day as well. So we would wake up early in the am to make reservation for the next day, but it was always “booked” not sure how??… when we were at the desk around 7:30am. We did get into the Italian and Mexican restaurant. Food was not that good except for the grilled octopus at the Italian. The Mexican blue agave was nothing special except for the lamb chops. The meat ball was terrible! The service everywhere was always so slow. Waiter and staff were not attentive. Except when they notice you were tipping. We tipped since the beginning but there was no consistent staff. So we just felt ignored most of the time. Also when I say we tipped, we tipped well. Tipping shouldn’t be factor of level of service received since this is all inclusive, you should receive good service with or without tipping. Also, check in was terrible, we stood there for at least 30 min waiting on service. Multiple people working the desk, but no acknowledgment of the guest at all. Once again lack of service. Also there were very few spaces that were ac gathering area, so it was really hot most nights. Most resort has a rec room or multiple lounges with ac so the gust can relax this place did not. Just the sports bar. Which gets really loud with club music after a certain time. Which if that is what you are looking for then fine, but def not a place to just sit and talk and be able to hear a conversation.

reviews.author: Danny Perez
reviews.text:
I enjoyed our time on the beach especially with the excellent service provided by Marileisy. She provided us with excellent service and made our experience on the beach very enjoyable.

Our dinner at the wine club was excellent and our servers Johnathan and Juan provided excellent service. I will definitely have dinner there again.

reviews.author: Gregory Gatteny
reviews.text:
We would like to tell you how much we appreciate your time and efforts to get us on vacation. Thank you for Juan, the upgrade to the Reserve was the way to go, especially when it came to the food, the beach & the other pools.

Just a few of our thoughts: In our opinion, Definitely not a 4-5 star resort. We called down for ice and towels the first 2 days we were there, we received them without issue, after that we called down multiple times for towels didn't get them, we called multiple time for ice didn't get it. When it comes to Language and communication a 4-5 star resort should be able to assist and communicate with all there guests. Some staff spoke a little English but not enough to feel like we were understood.

When it came to the buffet at the Lunch Box, some of the items were labeled and some were not. Tourists with food allergies need to be careful, my wife has a gluten & shellfish allergy, when we asked about some of the food items at the buffet, I don't think the cook/chef tending the buffet understood us. There were so many people at the morning buffet that the 2 omelet/egg stations had 5-7 people deep in line.

The lounge chairs and tables at the main pool were broken, cracked and rusty. The main pool is in need of repairs. Every morning there was always trash around the pool deck, my wife stepped on a piece of plastic that would of cut her foot if she didn't have water shoes on.

We loss electrical power once and we loss the air conditioner twice. The second time the air condition went down was the day before we were leaving, the blowing of warm air soaked our floor with condensation, my wife slipped and twisted her hip. I called down to let them know, they said OK we will send someone up. I sat there for 2.5 hours while my wife & daughter were at the pool. I called multiple times and was told OK they are on it. This is were communication comes in, they should of said to me that they are having a problem with the main unit  so I didn't have to wait in the room.

The Resort had great views, but having to be shuttled to the beach, because the direct access was for Circle or Reserve members, pools closing at 7 PM and not opening until 10:00 am, all this information should be in the Resort Description so vacationers can make a better decision.

Again we appreciate Juan, we also met Leonela she is a concierge who we engaged with on our 3rd day there. I guess we were suppose to meet our concierge and have welcome drinks when we arrived, we didn't have any of that.

This was our experience, our thoughts and opinions. Thanks again for all that you did for us.

Jhonathan at the Winery made our last nite in Punta Cana Relaxing and pleasurable. After losing the air conditioner in our room, we headed down to the Winery for our last meal. Great meal great service. Thank you.

reviews.author: Michelle Kristofik
reviews.text:
While the location was beautiful, and restaurant staff were wonderful, the management and customer service was the worst I’ve ever experienced from an all-inclusive resort. We noticed they trick you into leaving 5 star reviews by asking you to review specific places after some drinks, but the link actually leads you to the whole resort, not for individual bars or experiences (Ismael at Ginger Cafe, I would leave YOU a 5 star review, but not the resort).

Upon arrival, they took my passports and payment, and left us standing around for about 15 minutes. The rooms were not ready until 2 hours after “check-in”. They kept offering to take our bags, but it was clear others were waiting around for hours without their bags and unable to enjoy the pool and beach. I’m used to being handed a drink at check in, given an introduction of the place, and ALWAYS a map to our room. Not here. We traveled with another family, and they also had a similarly poor check in experience.

When we left, they tried to double charge us. Despite me showing the charge from my bank with the hotel’s details, we were held 25 minutes past our departure time. It felt as if they were trying to hold us responsible for their ineptitude. We even asked our transport guy to just take us since we clearly paid and the front desk started to argue with him.

Otium, their primary transportation service, also failed to have our info at the airport upon arrival, nor did they have the confirmed time for the ride back when I was told to expect it.

I was also left confused by their food and if any of their chefs have even tried to look up videos of how to make international dishes.

With that said, the restaurant staff and activities team was always wonderful and a pleasure to interact with. The place was beautiful and the pools and beach were always clean.

But if they want to provide a 5 star experience, they need to figure out how to make check in and check out a more relaxing and welcoming experience— not the most confusing and stressful aspect of the trip.

reviews.author: Katie Simione
reviews.text:
Thank goodness for the amazing service here! Our concierge Nathanael has been spot on taking care of us  step of the way, going above and beyond! Our guys on the beach Martin and Rafael made our days on the beach perfect. They were ahead of our needs every day, set us up with the best spot, kept the drinks coming steady and cold, excellent service, go find them on the beach they will make your trip immensely better!
Things to improve - the food is just not good. Overcooked, flavorless just needs so much work to be good. All the buffets all the speciality restaurants were just NOT good.

reviews.author: Lisa Stewart
reviews.text: All things considered, the hotel should charge less or step up their game in terms of professionalism at the check in area and improve their food and drinks. My family did have fun, and there are many wonderfully polite and pleasant workers on the resort. The pool has really fun activities that change out each day and the architecture/view on the property is gorgeous. The beach was lovely, and it was a fun vacation with kids. We  came here for my husband’s business trip and I tagged along with young kids for vacation, so it’s definitely better than winter in New York, but some improvements could be made for sure.

reviews.author: amanda medina
reviews.text: Service was wonderful. Yaleidi, our concierge, was very helpful, punctual, and accommodating. Our room was very nice with an ocean view but there was an interesting smell in the toilet area that did not go away even after asking housekeeping to clean it. Location was awesome, we were right off the beach with an amazing view and super easy access to the beach. There was plenty of space on the beach to sit as we were there during slow season. One thing I would warn is that if you go during May there tends to be a lot of seaweed on the beach due to the season we heard.Food was a downer for us, but found that the best restaurant was the steak house as well as Sante on the adult section. Aside from food being very underwhelming, I can say we had a good experience and the service was wonderful. Please ask for Yaleidi if you can, she was truly a pleasure to work with.

reviews.author: Paul S
reviews.text:
When you book a 5-star resort, you expect a 5-star experience. However, after staying here, this is not a 5-star — it’s 3 stars at best.

While the rooms and facilities are nice and clean, the food and service are sub par. At a 5-star resort, the expectation is 5-star service, food, and facilities across the board. That is clearly not the case here.

From the start of our week-long vacation, we encountered numerous issues with our room. First, our bracelets, which serve as the room key, did not work. Once in the room, the air conditioning and TV remote did not work. We were also left in the dark with no functioning lights for an hour. It took three phone calls to resolve each of these issues. And to make matters worse, no one spoke English so it was nearly impossible to communicate our displeasure.

You also expect the food and service to be high end at a “5-star” — it was not. The food at all the restaurants was inconsistent while the service resembled your local Chili’s. Plus, even getting a reservation is a difficult process.

The perfect example happened on our last night. First, we had to wait 45 minutes to be seated at a table that was empty for those 45 minutes. Once seated, we ordered 12 total items (apps, soup, main, dessert), but the waitress said in Spanish that we were ordering too much. The manager then said to her in Spanish, they can order whatever they want. Neither knew that I could understand what they were saying, but as this is an all-inclusive hotel, you’d expect that conversation to never happened.

Beyond this, the language barrier was a huge issue as it almost killed my girlfriend. She has a soy allergy and when she asked for almond milk for her coffee, they brought out soy milk. If she had not verified before drinking, it would have been Cafe de Muerto (the coffee of death). When we brought this to the attention of the front desk staff, they essentially changed the subject and didn’t acknowledge that their waitstaff almost killed my girlfriend.

Also, it’s clear that the only reason this “5-star resort” gets such good reviews is because the waitstaff at some of the restaurants will stand over you with a QR code and ask you to write a 5-star review as they peer over your shoulder to see what you’re doing. No true 5-star resort would even consider this as a tactic. I’ve never felt more uncomfortable during an interaction at a resort in my life, so I politely declined.

On top of all of this, the casino isn’t on site and felt like I was gambling in my friend’s basement. With 12 slot machines, 2 blackjack tables, and 1 roulette table, the casino was more like a party room at a bowling alley instead of that of a 5-star resort.

My expectation at a 5-star resort is that everything is five stars. That’s clearly not the case here, but there are some positives. The rooms are clean and hotel is beautiful. There are also a few staff members who are diamonds in the rough. We found Rodolfo, a member of the concierge staff, to be extremely helpful. He was able to get us a reservation for 12 while our friends, who had a personal concierge, had no luck. Jose at the In Between bar, was kind and personable. After ordering with him once, every time we went back he asked if we wanted that same drink. That is the type of hospitality that you expect from everyone at a 5-star resort. The bartenders at the main pool bar and Ginger bar met our expectations.

All in all, the Paradisus Palma Real is a 3-star resort disguised as a 5-star. I wish there were more positives, as overall our vacation was saved by the beautiful beaches and perfect weather. I hope the Paradisus takes these real reviews into account and makes some changes in the future.

reviews.author: Jackie Landry
reviews.text:
Ricki at Lunch Box was very nice and helpful.
Osvaldo was our concierge. Was always available for questions. Very nice people.
Food could have been better.
3 star because of food… even 2 star
Beach was nice but not many waiters passing for drinks. Had to wait or go get our own.
Not enough towel locations.

reviews.author: Nat J.
reviews.text: Our room was amazing and clean, Our concierge was very helpful and attentive. One thing i have to say was that a day before you checked out they will have the presentation for you( trying to make you join the membership and it last about 3-4 hours!) so if you already knew your answer then… and you know why they want to have a presentation on the last day you stay? Because if you signed up..they will change your bracelets and  you only have 1 day to enjoy the “lobster” and “RibeyeSteak” and “unlimited wine lists” again no hard feelings but people know why. So if you want to become a member go ahead when you reached, JOIN then you have more time to enjoy the perks!

reviews.author: Lauren Thomas
reviews.text: My stay at this 5-star resort was sadly somewhat disappointing for a first time all-inclusive experience. It's evident that the positive reviews here are likely coerced, as the staff relentlessly hounded guests for good reviews right after serving them. Housekeeping also stole our tip for our personal concierge while we briefly left the room (for not even 2 minutes) and lied when confronted about it! (Luckily, our concierge got it back.)The location was beautiful regardless. Food and drinks were actually pretty good- so no complaints there! Lastly, our personal concierge was pretty helpful so that was a huge plus.

reviews.author: Laura Bigelow
reviews.text: I give this 3 stars, and the food doesn’t quite reach the same caliber as the service & rooms. Mediocre at best, whether eating at the buffet or in one of the many restaurants. Best restaurant was the hibachi, which I’d rather at a solid 7. Nothing blew us away as far as food went. And all inclusive drinks seemed WEAK, at best. Little to no booze, so stick to beer & wine if you want to make sure you get what you’re paying for.

reviews.author: Jerry Gumpel
reviews.text: Our butlers Alvaro and Kelvin were great. They were attentive to our needs and procured reservations for us every day at the time and place that we wanted. The food and beverage operation is below par and it’s a pity as the resort is beautiful, as is the beach.

reviews.author: Sam Migdal
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel.  Restaurants are pretty good.  Good luck getting a reservation at any restaurant.  They make it impossible to get any time at all then the next move to reservation available at 9:30pm.  Front desk is challenging.  That’s all I have time to say because there is no way to describe the ineptitude.  If you are lucky enough to check in and check out without issue, you may be ok.  Unless your keys don’t work for no reason.

reviews.author: Rajat Arora
reviews.text: Beautiful location and very well kept, but food was not really good at the buffet. Main buffet was closed 7 nights we were there, malwa buffet was cold and not many choices. Going to the beach was ruined by hawkers trying to sell stuff. You need to know Spanish because most staff don't speak English at all, but they were all nice and accommodating. Our host, Alejandro, was brilliant. Swim out room was the best part, pool was very clean and warm at all times.

reviews.author: Spiro Kasimis
reviews.text: The property itself is beautiful. The many pools and the beach are beautiful their service though is subpar. 9 PM reservations at one of the many restaurants to get you seated at 10:45 PM. Unacceptable. The food is subpar as well. Bottom shelf liquor not ideal first time we did all inclusive probably last time we ever do it. We ended up leaving the resort three times to get decent food.

reviews.author: Andrew Hjorth
reviews.text:
Very disappointed with our experience at this resort. The staff was very nice but very little English spoken, sometimes it was very hard to communicate when ordering food and drinks.

The beach area was very nice and beautiful, the rooms were clean and comfortable.

Now the really bad part. The food is awful. I’m not joking when I say this, a couple people in our party lost weight the four days we were here, not just a little bit. We skipped meals because we knew we wouldn’t want to eat bad food again.

reviews.author: Melissa Reitz
reviews.text: Overall I think this is a beautiful resort but misses the mark on customer service. However, the highlight of our trip was our dinner at Flora. Melina was a delight and the food was fantastic - the best of our trip!

reviews.author: Camillus Patel
reviews.text:
The property is beautiful…one of the best lobbies and common area, clean open rooms. I really appreciated that most of the common areas were open air with a view of the ocean. The pool was great although wish it had some more shallow parts that would make the pool bar more accessible for those of us who don’t like getting our hair wet in the pool every day.  The beach access was amazing.
My biggest frustration was the lack of clear information around upgrade to the reserve. I wish this information was more clearly available during the time of booking so that me and the rest of the group I was with (3 rooms total), could have made a better decision. The biggest challenge was trying to get any reservations for the restaurants. The system was that on Sunday morning reservations for the entire week opened up. So if you checked in on a Thursday you pretty much had no shot of getting a reservation at any of the restaurants, unless you had reserve upgrade. Most of the restaurants were half empty when we would walk by yet we were repeatedly told there was no availability. When Sunday came we were one of the first groups in line to try to make reservations for the rest of the trip including Sunday night. We were immediately told there was no availability for Sunday night or Monday night even if we split into two gyros of 4—-how can this be when we were literally the third group in line??? My sister patiently worked with the service rep to ultimately find us availability But it was like they were doing us a favor. We made it work but the amount of time and disappointment really took away from the overall experience.

The staff was really nice and helped if you asked a question; However, there was a element of personalized service that was missing. I think you got this if you upgraded to the reserve. For example if we were at the beach we hardly saw any service being offered. I needed help to book a return car service back to the airport and they had no information available and said they only thing they could do is book me a taxi…? Really?. So it was the small things that could’ve been better for a getaway that wasn’t exactly cheap.

That being said the property is beautiful the meals that we did get at the restaurants were great. The bartenders were always super friendly. I would probably come back but only if I can afford upgrade to the reserve (since I don’t know how much the upgrade is).

reviews.author: Holly
reviews.text:
Great setup for older couples without kids (no wildlife or anything to swim with).

Bar service is great, find Arisleida at the adult side of the beach. She will take care of you.

reviews.author: Brittney Sharp
reviews.text:
Marileisy was a wonderful sever throughout our entire stay. She was ready with drinks and remembered our orders all week long. She was bright, cheerful, and so helpful while we had a large group of 14 (including 5 kids, 5 and under!) Her service was a highlight of our stay!

Our main complaints were as follows: it was nearly impossible to get change. We were refused a purchase at the store due to lack of change (while they were counting change). It made it extremely hard to tip the valued employees. Second, the grounds music played constantly, all night long, and could be heard clearly in my room in the middle of the night. Restaurant service was generally good, as was the food, but we had a negative eating experience on the final night. Finally, we felt that the overall communication of the resort was confusing. The areas, restaurants, bars, activities, and that were available to our level of stay was unclear.

We appreciated the guest services manager’s assistance throughout our stay and Dalmis and Wily were very helpful.

reviews.author: Faith Schultz
reviews.text: Ebony yedy likes to give her own review of 5 stars after taking your phone under the assumption of using a translating app. Cant say that she earned it, she came to our table and asked if we needed something to drink. We didn’t receive the mimosas and the water had a fishy smell??! But Joan and kelvin were amazing!  We didn’t care for the scheduling of dinners at restaurants at the last hours. SCUBA is not worth the time or money as well as chartered fishing  The free catamaran was very enjoyable! The main pool bar was by far the best of the outdoor bars. Steak house and Mexican were the best food options  entertainment was marginal, except for the young Spanish singer at the Mexican restaurant and the 4 person band with a female lead singer and female lead guitarist. Overall this was a good vacation. ( ps. Wouldn’t buy into the Circle ownership)

reviews.author: Vanessa Fontoura
reviews.text:
We stayed at the resort on our honeymoon and unfortunately our experience wasn't the best!!

We split our trip between two resorts and Paradisus was the second one we stayed at.

I'll describe my experience in bullet points:

FOOD: Very poor, especially considering it's an all-inclusive Golf and Spa resort. I noticed that the food used at breakfast remained on the buffet all day, and in some parts, it wasn't refrigerated; they only changed the location where the food was prepared... we had food poisoning and spent an entire day in our room feeling unwell. The restaurants that required reservations for dinner were very weak compared to the other resort (Majestic Colonial, which I highly recommend, much better).

Deluxe Master Room/Suite: The room we stayed in was wonderful!!! The room had a kit with toothbrushes, toothpaste, soaps, shampoo, and conditioner – everything was very good quality!!

Room service: A disgrace! We only ordered fruit and they didn't even show up or give any feedback (we ordered because we were too unwell to leave the room).

Drinks: All the drinks were very good, and there was no need to tip, which is normal for Americans. I didn't feel any difference in service in that sense, nor in the quality of the drinks served.

Tipping: I didn't feel pressured to tip, but I felt that in the restaurants they treated Americans better, as they have the habit of giving a dollar or tips for service.

Pool: We felt that some of the pools were dirty.

Security: Second-class in several locations of the resort, a very good sense of security.

I didn't even take pictures of the place because we got sick and couldn't enjoy it!!

I recommend looking for another place because there are many other resort options!!!!

reviews.author: Jomar Harfuch
reviews.text:
What bothered me most was the number of smokers. You can't enjoy the beach and the pool with them. The smell of cigarettes everywhere.
I was also bothered by private side events that took place on the beach. Their sound interfered with the sound of the hotel's performances.
There are no snacks on the beach, however, it's an advantage because the sand stays clean.
There was one day when there was no hot water in the shower.
The food is quite varied, but it doesn't have the refined flavor of a bistro.
There is a need to develop a system so that guests don't reserve pool and beach chairs by placing a cap on the seat that stays there all day, like a parking meter.
As for beaches like the famous Saona, rampant tourist exploitation has ruined the natural landscape. There are many kiosks, chairs and boats on the beach.
Playing loud music.
In addition to seaweed. Saona Island is far away and not worth it.
The beach in front of Paradisos is also very busy.

reviews.author: Axel Vallée
reviews.text: I stayed at this hotel for five days. I wouldn't have stayed a day longer... the food, the service, and the location were all terrible. I absolutely do not recommend it. It's an all-inclusive resort that claims to be upscale, but it's all smoke and mirrors. Opt for an Airbnb instead, because it's not worth it. The value for money is disastrous.

reviews.author: Marisa Azevedo
reviews.text:
The hotel is very nice, clean, and pleasant. We had a good reception, but the services were terrible! It starts with the concierge service, which offers a differentiated service, but in our case, it was awful. The person who attended to us only had one interest: that we participate in the welcome meeting, which was nothing more than a sales pitch for a program of future stays. It was a pushy move, but it wasn't our intention, so we didn't sign up. However, we informed the concierge from the beginning that our intention was to enjoy the hotel, but that we would like to go to the city center sometime to stroll and explore, as we always do on our trips; since he said that this assistance service during our stay would be entirely provided by him, including transfers from the location to the hotel (at no cost). We loved the idea and arranged it two days before our departure. Not only did the transfer not arrive, but we lost an entire afternoon waiting, and "our concierge" had to leave because he had been called to a meeting. We were extremely upset. On the same day, before the day ended, "our concierge" sent a message apologizing and suggesting a new tour. I resisted because I didn't want to lose another day, and it was the day before our departure, but my husband convinced me, and we gave his booking another chance.
It was worse than the absence the previous day. The so-called Transfer van arrived, and I had to take a photo leaving the hotel, a photo upon arrival at the location, and a photo upon return (I felt like I was being proven alive). The place was awful; it looked like one of those bus stops, just two shops with horrible, overpriced products (all in dollars). We didn't even stay 15 minutes. We requested to return to the hotel. I was indignant, and when I questioned our "concierge," he said that everything was dangerous, which we postponed later with other people, and this is not true.
The hotel service is very poor. I will mention a few points:
They didn't restock our room's mini-fridge. I had to call reception, and they feigned ignorance and didn't deliver what you asked for.
The hairdryer in the room was completely disassembled and didn't work. I requested a replacement, and another one only arrived two days later because I kept complaining and demanding it.
One day, they came to change towels and clean the room at almost 6:00 PM because we arrived from the beach and wanted to shower. I had to film it and complain.
The bathrobes in the room that are offered for use during the stay were all there. I had one that I used, and the next day they collected it with the towels; it never came back.
Drinks (all inclusive) were difficult to obtain at the pool bar or during any nighttime event, as it seems they don't want to improve this service so as not to replenish what they offer as "unlimited drinks." We even got tired of waiting and ended up without drinks (terrible service).
There are some restaurants within the complex that require advance booking. We managed to get a reservation after 3 days, and at the reception during our check-in, they informed us that we needed to book from one day to the next. There are 4 available, but only one restaurant had a reservation, and that was two days in advance. We booked a table at an Italian restaurant and it was disappointing. I ordered black pasta with shrimp, and it was a horrible, spicy pasta, very bad… I only ate the shrimp, which were good.
In short, my thoughts are that the Meliá chain only wants to create “members,” as they called them. If you are a simple guest who just wants a good stay and good service, forget it, because these privileges are only for members. The reserved areas in the hotel with clearly better infrastructure are for members, the better restaurants, the better service with drinks, in short, everything is better for members. I preferred it when we were just guests.
Therefore, this magnificent and beautiful hotel is not a place I would return to, and I do not recommend it to anyone seeking accommodation without discrimination based on whether they are a member or a guest.

reviews.author: Plinio Julián Calvento
reviews.text: The hotel itself is excellent, but the overall service from the staff is poor. From the reception staff to the restaurant workers, the receptionists don't explain everything about the hotel properly, and the restaurant staff rush you to finish quickly. If you go during lunchtime or later, you always miss out on dessert. Friendliness and empathy are lacking; the staff needs more training. I would only mention the excellent service from Mr. Guillermo (the concierge), Mr. Gabriel, and the staff at Winnery.

reviews.author: Hector Fernandez
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real, in The Reserve area. The hotel, in general terms, is fine, but the experience clearly falls short of expectations for a Paradisus, especially when compared to other properties in the chain in different locations.

The facilities are attractive: the pools are spacious and very pleasant, the beach area has one of the least sargassum seaweed areas in the region, and the room is modern, clean, and comfortable. As for the food, it's quite good in most restaurants, with one clear exception: Flora, where the quality is noticeably lower than the rest.

The main problem with the hotel is the service and management. Our concierge in The Reserve, Gustavo, gave us a very poor welcome: he barely explained how the hotel worked or the available services. We had several problems with restaurant reservations, which we had made three months in advance and were still poorly managed; we requested changes, and only one was corrected. Furthermore, the 23rd was our anniversary; we informed them beforehand, and they completely forgot. The gift arrived two days late, on the 25th, which completely undermines the gesture.

The minibar is restocked irregularly and incompletely, which is inconsistent with the hotel's category and the concept of The Reserve. During room cleaning, the doors were left open on several occasions, which is inappropriate from a privacy and security standpoint. Furthermore, the air conditioning system was quite noisy, disrupting our sleep.

The staff, in general, is friendly, but they clearly lack training and organization. The reception at The Reserve deserves special mention; the service is cold and unwelcoming.

As an additional negative point, the hotel's shuttle service is not operated directly by them, but by a third party, and its management is poor. They are inflexible regarding flight schedule changes, and despite being presented as a booking benefit, the hotel completely disclaims any responsibility for any issues, which is particularly disappointing for an establishment of this caliber.

We've stayed at many Meliá hotels, especially the Paradisus and Gran Meliá, and unfortunately, this one falls short compared to other properties in the same brand. It's a decent hotel with good facilities, but the management and customer service don't live up to expectations for the price and category.

reviews.author: Emmanuel Pedra
reviews.text:
We were on a family trip, and honestly, the hotel's food, entertainment, and beach were top-notch. It was the best beach in the area, as far as we could walk.

The problem was with the service and the assigned concierge. We had a reservation through Expedia, which gives you some extra benefits, like complimentary Corona beer. The thing is, no one explained this to us; we had to figure it out on our own. No one seemed to know.

The other problem was our assigned concierge, Rossmary. She showed a complete lack of interest in customer service, did whatever she wanted with our restaurant reservations, and never cared about our preferences. When we expressed our dissatisfaction, she immediately cut off communication, and whenever we crossed paths at the hotel, she looked the other way. It was shameful of her. My recommendation: even if you're assigned a concierge, try to handle things yourself.

reviews.author: Agustin Reynoso
reviews.text:
I stayed at this hotel just a few days ago to celebrate the New Year.

"The hotel is all-inclusive." In terms of infrastructure, it's very good, and the facilities are very comfortable and clean.
What I didn't find convenient was that I paid $700 USD per night for something that wasn't truly all-inclusive. There were no signs indicating areas where access was restricted, and at one bar, they wouldn't serve us drinks because we didn't have a membership, which is very expensive for a once-a-year trip. On the beach, it cost at least $250 USD to park your belongings on a bed with a torn and very ugly top.

In the area that was supposedly included, they tried to charge us $70 USD, which was cheaper, but still not fair, and there were no signs indicating this, so the staff had to rush us around, which was a very disappointing aspect of the experience. The service at the bars is only good if you speak English and tip more than $5 USD per drink. Because we are Latino, we weren't greeted on several occasions. At the 90 Degrees bar, Mr. Alberto made a distasteful comment, which I understand was a reference to the homophobia some people at this hotel have. Similarly, at the Ginger bar, Mr. Miguel started cleaning the bar, which was already clean, both times we went to order drinks.

An unpleasant experience. In contrast, Luis, from the same bar, spoke to us very cordially and tried to alleviate our discomfort. Room service has a menu, but when you pick up the phone, nothing is available. They don't deliver alcohol to the room, and I waited until my departure for some ice I requested, which never arrived. They only delivered ice made with water. The minibar wasn't fully restocked; it didn't cool properly, and out of five days, it was only restocked twice because we called. Every time we complained, they pretended to listen and said they would take steps to improve, but clearly they didn't, because it kept happening.
The restaurants inside the hotel aren't what they seem. We went to the Asian restaurant and they served us rice with meat and chicken. There's more variety at the buffet.
And when we arrived two nights in a row, we couldn't enjoy these places because reservations are required two days in advance, and no one informs you before your arrival so you can at least make a choice and they can reserve your table.
When we passed by those places, they were empty, and even then, we couldn't have dinner until the third night.
There's no control over the towels, and most people used up to five just to lie down and then left them wet in the same spot. I recommend bringing your own towel to avoid the unpleasant experience of walking around wet all over the hotel. I don't want a response to this comment highlighting how good their service is because there are many things that need improvement, and I hope they take action instead of just writing a long, drawn-out response from behind a machine. Maybe we're all being politically correct these days. While the secluded The Reserve area seems better, this isn't the case because someone I know who's staying there agrees that the service, in terms of price and quality, has a lot of room for improvement.

To top it all off, on New Year's Day I asked for two glasses and they told me that ALL of them—yes, ALL of them—were allocated to a beach event with a minimum charge of $180 USD per table. This means a hotel as large as this one doesn't have enough glassware to cover everyone. I've attached a photo below of the two glasses they couldn't bring me; they were at the hotel staff bar.

reviews.author: Raul Perez
reviews.text: Delighted with the service and attention from Emily and Lizardo. It's a real treat to have such helpful, kind, friendly, and above all, serious and professional people on your staff.

reviews.author: Eliana Paez Salinas
reviews.text: It's not worth the price; many services are charged separately on top of the already high cost of the stay. The facilities are top-notch, but the staff leaves much to be desired compared to other, less expensive resorts. The main dining room was very disorganized, and the staff didn't respond adequately to requests.

reviews.author: Jose M Guerrero
reviews.text:
My stay at the Palma Real this year was a mixed experience. At the breakfast and lunch buffets, the staff was very indifferent. It was difficult to order anything, and it was rarely brought. On other occasions, there was no service at all. We were promised that upgrading to swim-up rooms would give us access to the Grand Cana water park at no extra cost, which turned out to be incorrect, and in the end, we couldn't enjoy that amenity due to a lack of information. This is something management should take into account and provide better training for the staff to offer better service. Shout-out to Ricky and Junior at the buffet, who always provided excellent service.

On the other hand, we had a unique experience visiting Kicks. The entire staff—Jose, Yeimi, Altagracia, and others—always greeted us warmly, chatted with us, offered us drinks according to our preferences, and the atmosphere was always pleasant. It was the best place to be in the evenings after the main show.

Anthony always welcomed us with great energy at Ginger. Great conversations, excellent coffee, and lots of laughs in the afternoons.

Sandra always left our room spotless and provided excellent service.

I congratulate the staff who are doing a great job and encourage them to continue providing such excellent service.

reviews.author: RAUL POHL
reviews.text:
We had a wonderful few days at Milá Palma Real.

The beach was beautiful, the rooms comfortable, and the service on the beach, especially with Martin, was excellent—very attentive and friendly.

Emmanuel, our concierge, was fantastic.

The only downside was the food and the service in the dining rooms. The staff were always grumpy and indifferent. A major drawback.

Regards,

Raul

reviews.author: Tatiana Avalos
reviews.text:
Our stay at the Paradisus Palma Real wasn't the best. It was our fifth time with the Paradisus chain, as we've been to the Paradisus Cancun four times (and if we've been there so many times, there must be a reason). From the moment we arrived, no one escorted us to our room; we had to walk a long way in the rain without even knowing the place, since it was our first time. The food, in general, isn't good. The buffet lacks variety, and the lunch they usually serve near the pool as a snack is always in direct sunlight, which isn't good from a food safety perspective. In fact, some people got food poisoning because of it. The service, in general, is listless and unhelpful; you can tell they don't want to work. We saw many hotel employees practically doing nothing, just wandering around. Another issue is that the staff are pushy and rude. For example, on the beach, the vendors are very insistent on selling you activity packages, so much so that if you move, they move too (bordering on harassment), and they don't leave you alone. And in general, the beach vendors are very annoying and persistent. I don't know if they're just in this section of the hotel or in several hotels, but they should limit their numbers because you can't enjoy the beach peacefully without being approached every ten minutes with someone trying to sell you something. In fact, many times we had to leave the beach for another area because it became unbearable, preventing us from enjoying a full day there. Another incident involved one of the employees at the 36 Degrees bar asking me for a review. He was standing next to me watching me fill it out and touched my phone to enter five stars in the different categories, imposing a rating I didn't agree with.

I must admit that the facilities are very nice and spacious, and the evening shows are enjoyable.

They also have a Circle members' area that's practically deserted. I imagine it's not a very popular membership, so the place was always empty and the employees were just standing around looking at each other. I think that, at the hotel chain level, this membership doesn't seem profitable or strategic enough to justify having a dedicated space for it. They could use that space to offer the other guests a different way to enjoy it.

The service in general isn't good, to be honest. Sometimes you have to ask for things or sort things out yourself because the employees often demonstrate incompetence. If I were to return to the Dominican Republic, I wouldn't stay at the Paradisus again.

reviews.author: Abraham G. Ornelas
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, the overall service throughout the entire place, with a few exceptions, is very poor. In the restaurants, the food preparation and quality are terrible. The only redeeming features are the facilities and the Flora restaurant; the service there is good (we were served by Melina). The restaurant's theme is Dominican and fusion cuisine.

The perception is that, since most of the tourists visiting the place are not American, the initial attention and service will not be the best. Although the hotel claims that tips are already included, it's practically a requirement to leave a tip, preferably in dollars, because even Dominican pesos are poorly received, and this is noticeable from the moment you arrive at the hotel until you leave. In short, if you don't make it clear that you will tip, you'll be practically invisible in this place.

On the other hand, it is very uncomfortable that, being a HIGH-CATE HOTEL, at any moment someone approaches you, whether it's the person who gives you the towels, walking around the facilities, or even when booking something at a themed restaurant; at all times they want to sell you some service or activity. It is truly uncomfortable and pathetic.

reviews.author: adriana piccioli
reviews.text:
Beware! At Meliá Wellness, they wouldn't let us leave unless we paid for what we had already paid for. One day, due to a flight advance, they kept harassing us about our remaining days until we had to pay to leave... A total rip-off. The place itself is excellent, and the service is very good. The staff is impeccable.
Yesterday, my family arrived from the Paradisus Palma Real. The comfort and ambiance were excellent. However, the buffet service was terrible. We would finish eating and there would be no drinks, only warm Corona beer. The water was also warm. The chain is in a very bad state.

reviews.author: Jair Luque
reviews.text:
The hotel is very nice overall and very new. It's clear they've done a great job with the design and follow the Meliá architectural style. The Reserve area is worthwhile, as it's the only way to get a decent meal at this hotel. The rest, specifically the dinner service, is dreadful, both in terms of the service itself and the quality of the food. There are many restaurants, but none offer acceptable quality for what they advertise. They're also very noisy.
The pools, entertainment, and beach service are excellent.

reviews.author: Renato Cornejo Jarufe
reviews.text:
The facilities were very nice, the room service was good, and the staff at the beach and pools were very helpful.

However, three out of five people working in the restaurant area were unhelpful; their initial response was "no," and you had to insist to get them to consider alternatives.

Finally, don't go in large groups; they raise many objections to reservations at the à la carte restaurants when the groups are 20 or more people.

reviews.author: Ody Peña
reviews.text: As for the food, the chef deserves two or three Michelin stars. However, regarding the service, I must say that Ana Michel deserves a special distinction that recognizes her dedication and efficiency because she is excellent and knows how to make people smile. Congratulations, excellent service, excellent food at Restaurant Flora.

reviews.author: José Luis Batista
reviews.text: The security team at the main gate, hiding behind the "motto" that it's for the safety of the guests, provide TERRIBLE service, denying entry even when you are the one bringing them the customers.

reviews.author: Cesar Lechuga Carreño
reviews.text: It has a good location, and the rooms are nice and modern, just like the hotel itself. The beach is very good, and the pool is too. The hotel service is average; customer service needs improvement. It's worth noting that Jordan was very helpful in planning a romantic dinner and kept us updated throughout our stay—excellent service from her!

reviews.author: Marco Uriel Téllez Bache
reviews.text:
The hotel is incredible, but they don't explain that restaurant reservations are booked up until three days later. I only stayed two nights, and neither of them allowed me to dine at an a la carte restaurant, only at the buffet.
And I think they need more events at night, something more lively.
The DJs only play music for gringos.

reviews.author: Felix Häfner
reviews.text:
We just left after 8 nights. First of all, the positive: the location is great, and the hotel and the grounds seem to be very well-maintained. The excursions are a lot of fun and definitely worth seeing, such as Saona Island. The cleaning lady also did an excellent job.

Now, unfortunately, we come to the bad part.

We arrived late in the evening; there were apparently problems with our room, so we didn't get ours until after dinner. Even after dinner, there were problems because the man at the reception didn't know what the problem was and apparently didn't understand English, so after trying to get to our room, we had to run back to the review.

The water in the room takes a few minutes to heat up.

We also almost missed our booked excursion because, despite our notification, the reception and the "bag boy" didn't tell the excursion driver where we were sitting in the lobby, and the driver drove away. With the help of an external excursion agent, he was able to call the driver back.

Unfortunately, most of the hotel staff don't speak English, which isn't a problem in principle, as 99% of guests are Spanish, but not all of them, so you might get the wrong drink, for example. Some of the staff are also super friendly and greet you with a friendly, genuine smile and do a great job.

The restaurants were mostly closed or only accessible by reservation, but there were no fixed opening hours, as the staff arbitrarily changed the times. Accordingly, we had the same meal every evening, which sometimes tasted average to sometimes poorly cooked, as, for example, the meat wasn't cooked well. At the bars, you couldn't drink the same drink for several days because certain products were apparently out of stock.

While we were at the pool, several hotel employees came up to us to offer us a free drink and then take a photo for the hotel. Unfortunately, I also experienced one time when the staff member wanted me to write a review, and he wrote the review himself in Spanish, highlighting certain names of employees I'd never had contact with. What's particularly confusing is that I don't speak Spanish and therefore couldn't write a review in Spanish even if I wanted to. He apparently didn't care.

I also had ear problems due to the seawater, etc., so I went to the shop inside the hotel. The staff there apparently had no idea about their products and referred me to the reception. The person at the reception asked a pharmacist to bring over some medicine, which, unfortunately, turned out to be overpriced.
Which, at the time, didn't matter to me.

One evening, my girlfriend cut her butt in the middle of the pool because of the sharp edges. So we had to see the hotel's doctor.

She was treated well there, but we haven't received any compensation yet.

It's especially important to note that small children also play in this pool.

Since our flight didn't leave until the evening, we had to pay an additional $20 per hour to stay in the room, despite what happened.

Overall, I wouldn't recommend the hotel because some of the staff are misplaced, and the service provided doesn't live up to what you'd expect from a 5-star hotel, especially not for the price. Furthermore, the sharp-edged pool should be closed and renovated.

reviews.author: Nevena Jovanovic
reviews.text: Incredible beach, impeccable beach service. Ramón, a very attentive waiter! He's incredible! Best stay since meeting him. I recommend you run into him on your beach chair.

reviews.author: vanessa rodrigues
reviews.text:
Beautiful place, wonderful hotel architecture, spacious, modern and clean rooms!
It's a shame that the service is far below expectations. Many tired and impatient employees. Food is also far below reasonable. Some dishes are okay, in the buffet, desserts are almost inedible.
The gastronomy is very bad, really weak. Restaurants at night have problems making reservations and are far from the standard seen in good resorts in Brazil. There is no service on the beach, you have to get it at the bar, and that's only for drinks. There are no snacks of any kind on the beach or anywhere to get them. Very few attractions for children.
We will not return!

reviews.author: S
reviews.text:
In our opinion, the two best things about the hotel are its facilities (completely renovated less than a year ago), and the fantastic room, as well as its proximity to the beach. The hotel is very committed to keeping the beach free of sargassum and provides good security for your peace of mind. However, in my review, I want to highlight many things that need improvement, especially in a 5-star luxury Meliá hotel where a night costs a minimum of $350 USD.

The food needs significant improvement, particularly the dinners at the restaurants. We felt ripped off. Serving such poorly prepared and low-quality food is unacceptable; it's not up to the standard of a hotel of this category. I'm not referring to one restaurant in particular; this happened in all four we tried, especially the Japanese restaurant, where we practically left our plates untouched. The Mina restaurant has very poor management. We ordered a hamburger and a steak, and it took an hour and a half to arrive at our table, with tremendous disorganization and a terrible reception area. These are unacceptable issues for a 5-star hotel.

What also struck us most was the staff service (only the waiters at the pool bars were satisfactory). The rest of the staff were characterized by apathy. The quality of work should be prioritized over the number of people working. We felt like we were bothering them just by being there. Many looked the other way to avoid serving us, while others prioritized clearing a glass from a table rather than asking us, thus avoiding having to move. They try to be pleasant in anticipation of the tips you might give them for every action they take. It's an unpleasant and self-serving situation. This is a shame, especially considering that as a customer you've paid a fortune for an all-inclusive package. It should also be noted that staff should be more careful when dealing with or having potential arguments, as we found many staff arguing about schedules and actions to be taken.

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.text: The hotel is very nice, but the service is poor. For example, after 9:30 pm there's no food anywhere unless you go to your room and order room service, which takes an hour. They should leave some food available at least until 2 am, like many other hotels do.

reviews.author: Emiliano Navarro Planas
reviews.text: It was a pleasure to visit the Dominican Republic, my second time there. My friends chose the Paradisus Palma Real, and the front-line staff were incredibly kind. I truly appreciate the daily contributions of the entire staff; I can honestly say it's a service characterized by kindness and respect. I even told them one day that I felt exhausted by their daily efforts. I stayed from September 3rd to 8th, and not a single day went by without me enjoying espresso at the Ginger Bar. I also made sure to enjoy the beaches and the service, as well as the pool near the white bridge. I was so grateful for that. My concierge, Eriol Alix, was attentive to almost my every move, always willing to help, even with problems beyond his control. Thank you, Eriol, you made my stay so much easier. I stopped to greet many people along the way, and I was very pleased. The same goes for the staff at the buffet: Bety, Yuleny, Sandra, Luis, and Steysi. I never missed an opportunity to greet them. A smile was missing, thank you very much. At the Ginger Bar; Antonio Ramirez, Nereida Meggi Samaria - Clary, thank you for your kindness, I would like to return and I will keep it in mind. Thank you guys for everything you do. I hope the management takes into account the comments I made, thank you very much, keep up the good work... don't lose your joy.

reviews.author: S. T.
reviews.text:
The hotel renovation pleasantly surprised me; it turned out quite nice. The suite was incredible.

The location, right next to the beach, is a dream.
The breakfast in the room was quite meager, and they didn't bring what I ordered.
Reception doesn't answer calls.
In the buffet area, the staff is quite poor; they lack training in customer service, are always grumpy, lack enthusiasm and motivation, and are unhelpful.
While there are some staff members who aren't up to the hotel's standards, it's important to acknowledge the excellent service provided by those who make our stay much more pleasant and enjoyable.
At the buffet, Andrea Santana and Rossana are always very attentive.
The young man in the omelet and egg area, the one to the right of the door, in front of the desserts, is charming and has a contagious smile every morning.
On the beach, the incredible Hansel is impeccable at his job and has a charisma that many should emulate. And last but not least, Santos, the head of catering, who leaves no detail overlooked to ensure every diner enjoys their meal to the fullest.
Thank you to this wonderful team who made my stay unforgettable.

reviews.author: Gustavo Villarruel
reviews.text: The rooms and surroundings are truly amazing, quite clean and comfortable. The food was also good, with varied options every day. However, the overall service was TERRIBLE, even AWFUL. The culture of tipping should always be a reward for good service, but unfortunately, the staff expects a tip even for passing you a napkin, and if you don't tip, they ignore you, both in the dining area and the bar. In the bar, it even becomes a violent atmosphere because if you don't tip, they either completely ignore you or throw your drink or whatever you ask for at you. The treatment of tourists is simply hostile. As I said, tipping should be an incentive for exceptional service, not an obligation.

reviews.author: Narine Petrosjana
reviews.text: I'll say right away that if we had paid £3,000 for the room, I probably wouldn't have expected anything special. This isn't our first time staying at a Melia, but we usually end up at another one where it's only for adults. We paid twice as much. We checked in at 8 pm, the room wasn't ready yet, we were taken to him, but not the first time, because the person who saw us off mixed up our room twice, and on the way he broke our suitcase, it was funny), but with a child on the road, it's not very fun to go back and forth. The rooms are good. The beach is divided, and you are only allowed to use the white sun loungers. You'll be driven away from the others because they're already run by Melia Falcone. You'll also be kicked out if you've taken the first row of sun loungers because they're for Melia Members. The soft beds on the first line cost $69. There are 6 restaurants here, but only 2 are suitable for children, and they're so-so. The Italian is still okay, enough for the little ones to eat. The Mexican is terrible - we just returned from there. There are 5 free items on the menu, and then everything else is paid. The Japanese restaurant is also paid. The room for children is so old) as if it weren't in a 5-star hotel). The dining room where the breakfasts are delicious, but very small, not a big selection, you'll understand after 2 days of eating there. We have a 4 cm cockroach living in our room, probably came from the street. There was one there too, but it was bigger. By the way, there was no shower gel, hand gel, soap, or conditioner in the room. I asked them to bring some 3 times, but they only brought some for my hands. In short, think for yourself, but I would say 💯 no, I will never come back here again!

reviews.author: Pauline by Julia Fdez
reviews.text: I would like to see improvements in guest services, room service, and call response. The lunch buffet was of poor quality, except for the Italian and Japanese restaurants (which were excellent). On this occasion, the room had problems with the air conditioning, the safe never worked, and the mini-fridge didn't cool. We spent a very hot night in the room.

reviews.author: Cote Echeverria
reviews.text:
The hotel is wonderful, but the service is poor. It feels like the waiters don't want to work; they avoid looking at you when you want to order something, and we even heard them arguing several times.
The rooms are very comfortable, but you can hear EVERYTHING from the neighboring rooms.
The food isn't bad, but it definitely needs improvement.

reviews.author: Sebastian Zaffignani
reviews.text:
Because the service in most areas of the hotel was very pleasant, and the hotel recovered very quickly from the hurricane damage without affecting the guests. The service at the Kids Club, run by Martina and Emanuelle, was excellent. My children came back raving about them. The food at the Hydrogrill was incredible—the best ribs I've ever had. The service from Alba, Olvaldo, and the other chef was excellent.
There were several less-than-ideal details, both in the service from some of the bar staff and also, I think, on some days when we were confined, which wasn't good. The service on the beach wasn't very good either; it was filthy, even compared to the beach next door. They didn't provide much information about what to do. And I also think the hotel should have somehow compensated the guests who paid for their stay in full but didn't receive the full level of service they were charged for.

reviews.author: Mariela Paz
reviews.text:
The service was terrible. One night I couldn't sleep because of loud music. I called five times and it wasn't until 1:30 in the morning that they sent someone. It was a TV blasting in an unoccupied room.
To get a coffee in the morning, you have to wait until you finish breakfast, and at the pool bar, they were serving drinks with spoiled milk. A hotel that charges an expensive all-inclusive price shouldn't have these kinds of problems. The service at the sushi restaurant was awful; some waiters didn't even respond when you asked for something. The staff seemed more interested in tips than providing good service. Meliá Club members are losing more and more services every year. The renovation is a plus; the new pools are very nice.

reviews.author: Patricio Zambrano
reviews.text:
The buffet food was far below expectations after paying $200 per person per night. Overcooked pasta, bland desserts… among other things. The waiters were distracted and inattentive. One out of every three times I went to the buffet, I had to get my own drinks (including water) because the waiter didn't arrive or there simply wasn't one covering the area where we were seated.

At the restaurant, they pressured me to write a review in front of the waiter, which I found to be very unprofessional. It was almost as if they were saying, "Give me a good review or there will be problems."

The shower in the room leaked water under the door, soaking the entire floor. The toilet seat was also missing.

reviews.author: Nerea Duran Fernandez
reviews.text: The hotel is fantastic and the staff are absolutely lovely. There were a few minor details that disappointed me, but they certainly had nothing to do with them; they go out of their way to make you feel right at home. Thank you, guys, and congratulations on your outstanding professionalism. I'd like to give a special mention to Juan Carlos, our concierge, who was always attentive to every detail. And to Leticia, a waitress whose smile and natural charm made you feel at home—I wish I could always be served by a Leticia in the hospitality industry; I'd take her with me to any bar or restaurant in the world. And to Carmen, whom we already consider a friend, for always having the most wonderful smile and positive attitude, and for your incredible professionalism—we'll definitely be looking for you every time we return. Thank you for your care, your professionalism, your naturalness, and your kindness. And to Fernando, who approached us to offer a hotel-sponsored excursion and became a friend, it was a pleasure listening to you, learning about Punta Cana through your experiences, and feeling so safe and at home. I can't forget William and his car transfers; I wish he had always been our driver, not just in Punta Cana, but in life. Thank you for your smile, your enthusiasm, and the passion you bring to every trip. As someone who works at Meliá and in the tourism sector, I can only say that people like you keep the wheels turning and ensure that millions of guests choose Meliá as their preferred hotel chain for their vacations every year. Thanks to you, we will visit you again; you made the experience truly worthwhile.

reviews.author: Jose Luis Fernandez
reviews.text:
We arrived after 10 days at the hotel, and honestly, there are several things to check before going to this hotel.

On the Melia website, they advertise a luxury experience, but the truth is, it's far from that.

If you're traveling with children, you should know that the hotel isn't entirely for you, as it has many adult-only areas (mixed with the common areas) and areas for the Melia Circle Club, which are off-limits.

With a family, for example, you can only go to four themed restaurants.

As for adult activities, the hotel is practically nonexistent in that regard, offering very little compared to what other resorts, even those less expensive, offer.

Problem resolution was nonexistent. We had more than one problem, one of which involved a stranger entering our room because the door didn't close properly and was never fixed. The worst part was that the response was, "It happens more than we think." No one came to check on us or anything. In this regard, I'm grateful to José Sepulveda, who was the only one who showed a genuine intention to improve things. The rest, nothing. We supposedly spoke with one of the hotel managers, Wladimir R. (I don't remember his last name), but he offered zero solutions, zero contributions.

If you have children aged 12-14 and up, you'll bore them to death. I recommend other options.

Of the four themed restaurants we tried—Asian, Mexican, Steakhouse, and Italian:

The Asian one was a disaster, bad food and little variety.

The steakhouse, Mina, is the best, with delicious food and good service; Carlos Rincon, Orlando Morel, Miguel Mena, Kendy Castro, Olvi Almonte, Jesus Robles, and Jose Eusebio.

The other two were nothing special.

Things I appreciated:

While the buffet isn't very varied, the food is delicious. The service from some of the staff is also very kind: Sandra Combo, Yudit Ciprian, Rikie, and Daniel (the chef who sounds like Donald Duck) were always very kind to our son.

Kid Zone: the staff here are excellent. My 6-year-old son really enjoyed the activities (which aren't very well advertised by the hotel). You could see the care the staff took with children; here's a long list of people I want to thank:
Jesus, Sujeidy, Alexandra, Tania, Yessica, Jennifer, Johana Gonzalez, Marta, Johana Santana, and Yesmeidy. If I've missed anyone, please forgive me.

Jesus, it was great to meet you, buddy! Thanks for everything!

At the beach bar, a big thank you to Luis and Jorge's team, and to Arisleida and Teofilo at the pool.

Summary; The hotel doesn't deliver what it promises, but the problem lies with management. There's zero solution, zero interest in guest well-being. A serious question for them is, what do they understand by a luxury experience? What are they selling?

The people we mentioned are genuinely interested in ensuring you have a good vacation.

As an aside, the Melia Circle club is a complete waste of time.

Surely, the response will be, "Next time will be better," etc., etc., etc. Let me tell you now, they don't care. I told them so, and nothing changed.

Regarding the 4.8 rating, be aware that some people pressure you to give them a good review.

reviews.author: María Alicia Cabrera de Requena
reviews.text:
CELSIUS: excellent service, delicious drinks, thank you Victor and your team.
There's a craft workshop every day; they're all very nice, one of them is run by Yovanni.
Most of the waiters are very bad, except for one or two.

reviews.author: Digno Perez
reviews.text: Glorious (like Paradise), majestic (like the Royal Palm), pristine, glamorous, divine—it lives up to its name. Our impression is recorded as a visitor, not a guest. As a guest of the Meliá Caribe Beach Resort, our keen interest in exploring it, coupled with a misspoken statement—"you may make USE of any of the resort's facilities"—a semantic error initiated by the travel agency and repeated by reception, security, and other staff at both hotels, whom we consulted, led to an embarrassing experience. While enjoying drinks and the pool, we were asked to leave by Rikermy Ávila, the head of security and manager, in a completely unprofessional manner. There are countless ways to assist a guest without causing discomfort and without allowing any prior misunderstanding to leave them with the worst possible impression of such a distinguished hotel's service. We hope that better training for all staff and retraining for management will prevent other guests from experiencing such unpleasant situations. After all, we weren't infiltrators and we went to have fun, without bothering others.

reviews.author: Izaltino Bernardi Jr
reviews.text:
Many flaws for a hotel of this category. The pool jacuzzis don't work, they don't even serve ice cream to guests on the private beach, and the restaurant is always out of certain dishes.
The only point of excellence is the service from employees Emmanuel and Jose Maleteros, especially Franklin at the Sante restaurant.

reviews.author: María del Carmen Gómez F
reviews.text: Good stay but overall very poor service from the staff, except for Rosanna at the main pool. Too much sargassum and the pools and towels were dirty.

reviews.author: Krzysztof Iwanowski
reviews.text: Decadent and poorly maintained, the food was very mediocre for a place of this category, and the desserts were even worse. It's a shame because I stayed at the resort in 2007, and for me, it was the epitome of an ideal holiday hotel. But since then, they haven't renovated anything. The common areas are quite poorly maintained for a Meliá luxury brand. The room smelled so musty that I had to wash all my clothes upon returning. The only toiletries in the bathroom were shampoo, body lotion, and hair conditioner.

reviews.author: Vilma marmol ricart
reviews.text: My experience at that hotel was bittersweet. The staff was somewhere between excellent and average, the food didn't meet my expectations, and the room didn't match what I requested in the reservation made two months in advance. Overall, I'd give it 3 stars.

reviews.author: Antonio Fortnite
reviews.text:
A beautiful hotel complex, a fantastic beach, and Luis Dias from the swim-up bar is the best – very attentive and always in a good mood. The food in the main restaurant is disastrous. They try hard, but compared to other Spanish hotel chains, Melia is unfortunately disappointing. Plates are often not properly clean, and the food is cold. There's far too much American food: for example, hamburgers everywhere... Of the specialty restaurants, we cannot recommend Sal. The steaks were completely burnt...and the portions were tiny.

The price-performance ratio is completely off. We give the hotel complex 5 stars, the junior suite 4 stars, the beach (which is cleaned daily) 5 stars, cleanliness 3 stars, the food in the main restaurant and Sal – no stars, and the food in Vento restaurant 5 stars.

reviews.author: Marc
reviews.text:
Fantastic facilities, right on the beach, BUT:

- EVERYTHING operates on a tip basis. If you don't tip, you'll get bad service and expensive service. Heads up, Spaniards who don't know the local currency, bring USD!!

- Either "know" someone or be prepared to queue at 8:30 am to make a restaurant reservation for dinner.

reviews.author: Roxanna Gianini
reviews.text: The hotel was very nice. The rooms were fine, but the staff was sometimes slow and forgetful. Housekeeping was late (16 hours)...they forgot to replenish snacks, and room service was unreliable; you'd order food and drinks and get food and drinks. At breakfast and lunch, if you asked for salt, ice, or any missing cutlery, it would arrive late or not at all. Finally, some male staff members would take it upon themselves to make unsolicited comments about my appearance.

reviews.author: Odette McBride
reviews.text: Paradisus Palma Real is very beautiful, with a great location, and the service provided by the staff is excellent throughout the Reserve area: Jose, Franklin, Bladimir, Joaquina, Eduardo, Luz Villa, and Zuleica. Pedro, in particular, is also excellent on the beach. The staff makes you feel like family.

reviews.author: Lisset Cabrera
