Suite/King Bed: our room smelled like vomit but they would not move us because they said they didn’t have any other rooms available.  Our room did not have the king bed we reserved.  Shower: had absolutely no pressure in it and just trickled either cold or scolding hot water.  It took forever to adjust the dial every time.  The towels and robes were old and overused.  The toilet leaked heavily and after they "fixed it" it didnt flush in the morning.  The electrical cord was ripped out of the lamp on the table and remained "live" under the bed.   The balcony door did not have a functioning lock on it and remained unlocked all the time. Dinner reservations for 4 people were impossible to get in advance - there was not a single 7:30 reservation at any of the restaurants the whole week!  The Restaurants - the food was very mediocre, lacked any kind of presentation or sides.  Dinner at the Peruvian restaurant was very disappointing as well.  At one point they tried to "upsell" the lobster dinner for an additional $32 a person, we later noticed that they were grilling lobster tails in the buffet that evening - all you can eat for free - what a racket!  The drinks:  My husband ordered Grey Goose vodka with cranberry juice only to be “yelled at” by the bartender that our green bracelet does allow us to have Grey Goose This is not disclosed anywhere on their website.  Service at the Buffet - was a disgrace, we didn't have a waiter for the first 15 minutes.... if you order a drink, water or coffee there was a 50% chance you would get it. The staff just disappeared and didn't care much even though we tipped everyone along the way for all our meals.  TimeShare Presentation: they pushh their "Circle Membership" presentations  on everyone. Stomach virus:  all of us were having extreme stomach pain and diarrhea starting our 3rd day in the resort which continued for a week.  THE BEACH - this is by far the absolute worst part of the vacation. It is horrible, murky and full of seaweed. I believe that Melia/Paradisus and Expedia go to great lengths to hide the fact how big of a problem the seaweed is.  Nowhere on their website does it disclose this information this is an extremely deceptive practice which prevents the consumer from being aware of this tremendous issue.  Melia/Paradisus does not properly clean/manage the seaweed  The problem is that there are sea lice/fleas and tiny crabs that live in the seaweed.   I was severely bitten by these tiny fleas and crabs and had a terrible reaction and an incredible rash all over my arms, legs and feet.  This caused a lot of burning and itching and I was unable to sleep at night.  It completely ruined my vacation as I had to stay in my room for several days and treat it with a medicated cream. I feel that the resort/experience was not as advertised and is absolutely not a 5* resort.  I hope other travelers will be ware and choose a different destination.

reviews.author: Patrick Miller
reviews.text: I came with my family for a Christmas vacation, my family members are platinum member with paradisus Palma real. We have been coming to this resort since 2011. Since our first visit a lot has changed with the resort everything for the worse. From service to rooms and food. Our room was not safe and/or clean and they said they are all booked and there is nothing they can do. For 4 days they were giving us empty promises and telling us they would switch our room to their new hotel, circle grand reserve. In the end nothing was ever done. Please do not become a member of this hotel. Attached are the images of the room that I stayed in. Completely unsafe with exposed wires and mildew in the bathtub.

reviews.author: Andy Sharma
reviews.text:
Food is terrible at Italian place, other places are reasonable but not great
And there is cheap tricks to sell some Circle stuff to waste time and discriminate between guests
Not good activities as mentioned on website as website included all sites activities
80% staff do not understand English

reviews.author: Krystal Lopez
reviews.text: My boyfriend and i were on a company trip out here, we stayed at this resort for a week. In the beginning we thought we were in paradise our butler was amazing and the staff were awesome. Until our personal belongings got stolen from our condo that we were staying at this resort! My Louis Vuitton purse our Passport Wallets our GoPro camera and cell phones that were in the safe in the closet were gone! I Panicked and went straight to the manager of this resort and he was SO RUDE to us. He was shutting me up and putting his hand in my face and telling me that there was no way that his staff could have taken it. He called everyone that worked there through his ear device to let them know what had happened and sure enough when we got back to the condo with the manager an hour later because the manager had us in his office for about an hour. Our stuff was back in our safe with a different password that whoever stole our stuff made up. But it was SO WEIRD that the manager knew the damn code!! NEVER AGAIN ARE WE COMING BACK! and for safety cautions i wouldn't recommend this resort to public. Scariest time of my life!

reviews.author: Hernan M
reviews.text:
stay away from this place, they don’t disclose that the hotel it’s under construction up until you signed and paid for it, and only until you ask how to get to the beach. They will deceive you by giving you an “upgrade” to another hotel, “The Reserve” but that’s also a lie, it’s not an upgrade, it’s the only thing the have to offer.

The pictures in their website show a direct access to a big beach area, and in reality you need to take a golf cart to go to the beach, driving by the gigantic construction area the “Paradisus Palma Real” has turned into (see my side by side comparison pictures below). The beach area has been reduced to less than half of what it was, and you will relax, seating looking at the ocean with a construction site in your back, with the natural noise of tools, jack hammer, trucks and workers doing their thing.

As i said, don’t even consider Melia “Paradisus Palma Real”, the pictures you see in their website are showing a hotel and facilities that don’t exist anymore.

reviews.author: osvaldo palencia
reviews.text:
My experience at this resort was nothing short of traumatizing. I was with a group of tons of family and friends and ensure you that none of us will be coming back. My trip date was August 25th-29th of 2018.

Let’s start with the check-in process. We get to the resort where we had to leave our bags in a parking lot and then make our way to check-in. Upon getting to the check-in counter none of our accommodations were fulfilled. Things such as birthday ribbons and connecting rooms were not done. Most importantly, our room wasn’t even ready so the employee recommended us to the buffet.

Upon getting to the buffet I was very confused since no one took the time to explain it to me. Utensils are found on the table that you’re attempting to sit at. I was unable to find where to get a beverage as well. I was also told we could sit anywhere, until a employee came up to us and stated that the buffet table we were at was reserved. Upon telling her I thought that we could sit anywhere she stated that I could sit anywhere but there. Great explanation.

After the buffet I went back to check-in and the room was ready. I was told our bags would be there shortly. 2 hours later and our bags were still not in our room. I had to go to the front desk, ask for my baggage where they called it in and shortly thereafter my bags were delivered.

During our stay, the TV within the room didn’t work all week. At check out a room service employee knocked on our door and stated isn’t it time for you to checkout? Also the electricity went out multiple times during our stay. I couldn’t get WiFi unless I sat on the balcony and worst of all when our sheets were changed they weren’t dried appropriately and were still wet.

My worst experience of them all had to be the on site doctor. We went to the on site doctor the night of August 27th into the morning of August 28th. My significant other was dealing with an infection in her intestines possibly due to food poisoning. The doctor there was moving so lethargically and almost seemed upset we woke him up with our concern. Turns out that she needed medical attention at a local hospital. The doctor on site took about 1hr and 1/2 to print out different paperwork and mention different fees. He originally even told me that his medical evaluation which consistented of taking her blood pressure and temperature would be $235 and I would have to pay that upon checkout. I found that later to not be the case since the hospital billed me the $235 fee and following up with the doctor that was on site during the day. We curiously asked how much it would be to get an ambulance since the process was taking so long to get her some real medical attention and he mentioned that we don’t want to know because we can’t afford it. At that point I was speechless.

All in all, I was really surprised with the attention to detail and customer service experience. It was horrendous. Most employees seem to not even care. Please don’t bother responding to this review, I have no interest in what you guys have to say as your actions did not speak louder than your words. Thank you.

The same individuals, who were cleared by the resort, would accost us multiple times a day even though we asked to be left alone.
After returning home and noticing the fraudulent charges on our account we email the resort to notify them of the incident and made requests about how we'd like this resolved (we did this prior to leaving reviews so Melia could resolve this issue in private). We didn't receive a response from our first email and after following up the manager of the resort stated they're starting an investigation he would reply in short order with their findings. reviews.text: Updated - 12/15/2018. Like all places when they are new they're great. This resort is dated and in need of an overhaul. In short we were repeat travelers who will not be going back to Melia/Paradisus/The Reserve or Palma Real ever again! Beware of this sinking resort chain.

reviews.author: Liam Domenico
reviews.text:
The resort is a 10/10. The employees, every single one of them, from hostess, to bartenders, to housekeepers, to concierge, make the resort a 2/10.

This would’ve been a very pleasant vacation at an amazing property, but the employees make sure to not make you feel welcomed. The only guy that was welcoming was Miguel the bartender at the Rum bar. He gave us a smile, had the most positive vibe and was just great. I should also add that Patricia and Eva from the spa were amazing when providing their services.

Our “concierge” Adriel, never gave us a tour to the property. We had to walk to our room by ourselves after waiting for over an hour at the reception desk where he never showed up. We were told we would text us, he never did. I had to go out of my way and find a way to contact him.

If you’re not +50 and white, don’t expect good treatment. If you’re a young couple in your 20s, expect nothing but absolutely nothing. Mind you we came with the American Express program and had access to the Reserve. That meant nothing apparently. We waited over 30min to be brought a Diet Coke to Santé which is the “reserve” restaurant, but all three servers were too busy serving one table with 3 Americans, so we got up and left and instead, went to the general buffet at the other side of the property.

I would absolutely love to come back, and bring my mother, siblings and my wife again, but with the level of service from the employees, I don’t know if I want to swipe my card at this place again.

Employees here need to be trained on customer service. And be taught that a young couple is also capable and has the same resources as an older couple in their 50s. Times have changed. Start paying respect to younger people who also pay every single dime to be here.

reviews.author: Ash Rafipour
reviews.text:
Cliff’s Notes: good amenities and grounds, terrible service, worse food, go book at Secrets instead. Thousands of fake reviews - servers will ask you to write a review and mention their name, not sure if there is an incentive, but after the third time it gets tiresome. Wonder how many are real reviews..

If I could rate this resort lower than 1 star, I would. The only good thing about it is really the layout, the main courtyard, and the beach.

Everything else is comically bad or outdated. Let’s go down the list…

1. The food is bar-none, the absolute worst food I have ever had the (dis)pleasure of eating. You can only make reservations same day, and only one restaurant per day..

The steak house (Mina) AT BEST is below average. Thin cuts, poor quality beef, impossibly tiny sides and appetizers (one empanada about a third the size of a pizza pocket, really???). Terrible wine selection unless you’re paying hundreds out of pocket. Service is sub-par, waited 45 minutes for my drink after reminding the server twice and he finally brings out two for some reason, with my dessert no less.

The lunch buffet is stale, bland food. The fruit has no flavour, meat is overcooked, but again… the service is below average at best. I sat there with my plate of food for 15 minutes before I got offered a coffee or a setting and utensils, had to go grab it off the cart myself.

Flora was okay for appetizers, but we waited 52 minutes (I counted) before we gave up and left since our main courses hadn’t arrived yet.

2. Service quality generally speaking isn’t great. I went to the front desk twice in an hour to request an ironing board (never arrived), and I had to go all the way there because the phone in the room doesn’t work…

The one highlight is the Cabana service, but then again we’re tipping $5 USD every interaction so it makes sense they’re constantly hovering around.

I think another review summed it up great: it’s an “I guess I can eat that” property, not a “I want to eat that” property.

3. Rooms are outdated. Almost no clothes hangers, terrible room service (sensing a pattern with the food?), air conditioning cools the room but just keeps things moist. Seemed like they need to drain the water. No garbage can in the room outside of the toilet room, so you’re constantly running back and forth.

In summary, spend your money elsewhere.

reviews.author: L P
reviews.text: Do not stay here. The workers are liars. The customer service is sub par. The resort is new and the rooms are nice but service leaves a lot to be desired. If you request any changes to your reservation make sure you get them in writing. No waiter service by the pool or beach. No food service by the pool or beach either. We booked directly through the hotel and stayed on the reserve side. Our butler / concierge made dinner reservations for us at times we did not prefer however the dinners were good. Room service menu is limited. The fridge in our room did not work all week and all they offered was an ode bucket that remained on the table all week after melting the first day. The hotel is not very crowded and no where near at capacity. Check in took forever despite having private check in at the vip suite. Skip this place and find somewhere with staff that is more accommodating. Rooms didn’t get cleaned until 530 one night. Finally got wash cloths on our last day. After our two hour check in, we were taken on a tour of the resort and when we finally got to our rooms our bags still weren’t there. Slow service. Stay elsewhere. Also you can’t turn the AC below 69F but the room only ever gets to 74F. Everything was very damp in our room.

reviews.author: Hélio Tatsuo Yostsui
Dede C
reviews.text:
My partner and I have seen quite a bit of the world and will see more, but we won't be staying at a Melia again after this experience.

We booked through the website (where a fantastic room was advertised), but then came the shock when we saw the room. The picture and reality were two completely different things – opening the balcony door revealed a strong smell of a deep fryer. At night, it was so noisy (a fan outside the hotel room) that we couldn't really sleep.

We went to reception and explained that we hadn't booked this room and that we were dissatisfied. We were then told that there were no other rooms available. Friendliness and helpfulness were nonexistent.

We then showed the receptionist that our Melia app showed plenty of rooms available – the response: that was a false display.

Even if this were true and the entire hotel was fully booked, we would have at least expected some friendliness. It was clear that the staff didn't care at all and couldn't have cared less whether we were happy or not.


We were told that we weren't happy or helpful. There are restaurants, but they're booked up 3-5 days in advance – so the noisy cafeteria is the only option.

The beach is the best thing about the hotel. The staff there aren't exactly friendly, but at least the beach is beautiful.

There were sun loungers (already quite old), but the nice ones shown on the website are, of course, only available at an extra cost. Around us were people with coconuts (also featured in the hotel photos) – when you ask the staff, half of them know nothing about the coconuts, and the other half charge between $5 and $10 (in US dollars) for one.

We've never experienced such service before.

This was the first time we've ever left a hotel early and booked a different one.

Even though we have many years ahead of us, we'll never set foot in a Melia again.

reviews.author: Marcela R
reviews.text:
THE WORST HOTEL EXPERIENCE we've ever had. Belongings disappear and they keep your money.

My boyfriend and I went for our anniversary, and by the third day, I already wanted to go home.

We booked a room in the adults-only section, and when we arrived, they told us they didn't have any available. They tried to move us to a "better" room in the family area. We found a jacuzzi with mold and broken doors. We complained, and they sent us back to the adults-only section.

When we got to the room, it smelled damp. We complained again because I have asthma, and we both suffer from migraines, but they said they couldn't do anything. We wasted EVERYTHING on the first day because of all this. To avoid ruining the experience and hoping for better service, we decided to upgrade to The Reserve. THE WORST DECISION.

From the first day, the concierge didn't even come to greet us. We had to seek him out multiple times and constantly chase him down to get him to pay attention to our restaurant reservations and other inquiries. That "exclusive" experience they advertise is pure fiction.

On the third day, my boyfriend left some belongings on one of the beach lounge chairs while we went to breakfast (a stainless steel cup, a book, and some sandals), as he was told he could do early so we could have a peaceful breakfast. When we returned, the sandals had been moved, the cup had disappeared, and there were other people in the chairs. We complained, and security said they hadn't seen anything, nor had the waiters.

We were put in touch with Laura from guest services/supervisor who, after trying to blame us, finally agreed to look into how to help. They offered us a couple of experiences for our anniversary and a refund for the two nights of the upgrade we had paid for. This was on April 17th.

On both the 18th and 19th, we reiterated to her and the concierge that they should please leave the refund request at reception to avoid any problems. When we checked out, with our transportation waiting, they told us they knew nothing about it. We finally found her, and she told us it was already being processed and not to worry.

TO THIS DAY, WE HAVE NOT RECEIVED ANY PAYMENT, ANY REFUND, ANY MESSAGE ADVISING US OF WHAT HAPPENED. WHERE IS OUR MONEY? We have sent emails, called, even written to the concierge, and NO ONE has responded. I had to write this hoping that someone will deign to pay us.

In short, do not stay at this hotel if you are looking to relax, feel safe, have a good experience, and receive good customer service. The food is so bad that there were days we preferred not to eat. The rooms are very poorly cleaned. You have to ask for everything multiple times. Room service is nonexistent. The vast majority of the staff have a very bad attitude. The service is mediocre at best, and the only redeeming feature is the beach bar, which provided excellent service.

reviews.author: Juan Jose
reviews.text:
First, I should mention that I've stayed at several Paradisus and many Meliá hotels, and this one was a huge disappointment.
The only good things about the hotel are the location, the size of the rooms, and the fact that it's not overcrowded.
We booked the highest category, a master suite.
The worst things, without a doubt, were the following:

1) Breakfast, lunch, and dinner were terrible. The dinners were so bad that it's better to go to the buffet than to the specialty restaurants. That says it all.

2) The service was the worst I've seen in 25 years of staying in Caribbean hotels, and that was even when it wasn't full. It's so bad that even having tea at breakfast is practically impossible.

3) The room was large and supposedly luxurious, but it turns out there's no water pressure in the showers, nor any hot water. The TVs didn't work. Unacceptable. After complaining repeatedly, they didn't offer a solution.

In short, I can't understand the good reviews.

reviews.author: Dzhuletta Uenal
reviews.text: Unfortunately, our stay at the hotel did not meet our expectations. The service was generally poor and inattentive. The room was not cleaned thoroughly enough; it was clear that the cleaning was not done carefully. The air conditioning had an unpleasant odor, which spread throughout the room. Additionally, there was no hot water for showering on several occasions, which is unacceptable in a hotel of this category. Overall, we were disappointed with both the service and the condition of the room.

reviews.author: Domingo Martinez
reviews.text:
At The Reserve, we arrived at 3 PM, checked in, and only at 7 PM, after searching several times for the concierge who never showed up, were we given our room. They gave us various explanations for the four-hour wait and the loss of our first day of vacation. The reality was that the room had a late checkout, meaning it had been booked twice. During our three-night stay, the concierge could only find us a restaurant for dinner at 6 PM, even though we had lunch at 3 PM! The 7 PM and 8 PM seatings were never even half full, but they claimed there was no space.
On our departure day, we flew at 8 AM, so we were leaving the hotel at 4 AM. The day before, the concierge had promised to order breakfast in our room, but the night before, we were informed by the lobby staff that they were full and asked if we could have a coffee in front of the lobby. At 3:00 AM, after calling three times to request luggage transfer, we went to breakfast only to find out the bar hasn't been open at night for six months, and there's no other bar in the hotel open at that hour. We left fasting and as bitter as the first day they made us waste our trip by not giving us a room. We've been traveling to Punta Cana with our children for 25 years, but this year, as we celebrate our 50th wedding anniversary, we decided to travel alone and change hotels. I wouldn't recommend this hotel to my worst enemy. Zero points for administrative service!

reviews.author: David Caro
reviews.text: I go to different resorts every year, and this one has some of the worst service relative to the price per night in Punta Cana. Look for other options, which will surely be cheaper. Here are some specific incidents that happened to me during my stay: they forgot room service orders more than once, you have to ask for everything two or three times, everything takes at least an hour, the restaurants have terrible service, and the best they do is apologize instead of taking action. As for the rooms, they are very spacious, however, the cleaning is poor, and the beds leave much to be desired. My mini-fridge was broken, and it took them four days to replace it, after multiple daily requests. There are many resorts in the area; look for one that doesn't belong to the Paradisius chain and where they care more about the customer.

reviews.author: Camila Zimerman
reviews.text: If you want to feel awful, come here. The service is truly disastrous. They don't even look at you, you have to ask for things (like water) a thousand times and they still don't bring them, they pretend not to notice, they treat you badly. I've never seen anything like it. Everything you want to do is a struggle. "All-inclusive"—try getting a glass of water... it's truly appalling what we're experiencing. I regret it so much; it's the complete opposite of relaxing. Everyone's complaining and they don't care in the slightest. A terrible experience. You spend a lot of money and have high expectations for your vacation and you're met with this. I'm speechless. A TOTAL DISASTER

reviews.author: Elias Pianko
reviews.text:
We spent ten days at the Meliá Paradisus Palma Real, and the stay was a disaster from beginning to end. For a hotel advertised as 5-star, the level of service is simply shameful. I think they buy fake reviews!

The only positive point is the setting. The hotel is very beautiful, and the outdoor areas are pleasant and well-maintained. Unfortunately, that's absolutely the only thing worth mentioning.

From the very first days, the staff's behavior was problematic. In general, the employees are cold, unpleasant, and constantly give the impression that they are being bothered. On two occasions, at reception, an employee literally breathed in my face after a simple request for information about a late check-out. This kind of attitude is completely unacceptable, especially in an establishment of this caliber.

The hotel restaurants are another major source of frustration. On two separate occasions, we waited forty-five minutes before anyone even took our order, and then another hour and a half to be served. There were only three of us, and the hotel was clearly not full. Such slowness is unacceptable and demonstrates poor organization.

Before our arrival, we made a single, very simple request: a room with a pool or sea view, an option included in the room category we had booked. The hotel wasn't full, yet this request was ignored, without any explanation or compensation.

The laundry service was one of the worst aspects of our stay. Upon arrival, there were no bags or forms in the room. We had to call reception three times to get them. Once we had filled out the form, we called twice to have someone come and collect the laundry, but no one came. The next day, they finally arrived more than thirteen hours late, which meant the laundry couldn't be returned within the promised twenty-four hours. I had to call three more times. In the end, the whole situation dragged on for four days, and I washed clothes for nothing since I was leaving the next day. A completely disorganized and inefficient service. 100 euros paid for this service.

On the day of our departure, our flight was delayed, so we asked to stay in the room for two extra hours. The hotel was almost empty. Despite this, we were asked to pay, and no compensation was offered. No understanding, no flexibility, no consideration for the customer.

Another shocking point: the staff systematically refuse to speak English. They understand it perfectly well but deliberately respond in Spanish and force guests to speak in that language. For an international hotel claiming to be 5 stars, this is simply unacceptable.

Finally, the room wasn't even properly equipped. There was neither an iron nor a hairdryer upon our arrival. After three calls to reception, the equipment finally arrived two days later, and even then, only a hairdryer, without the requested iron.

This stay was a series of problems, delays, and inappropriate behavior. The service is unworthy of a hotel of this standard. I strongly advise against staying at this establishment. There are much better hotels in Punta Cana, for less money, and with a genuine commitment to customer service.

reviews.author: Jose Antonio Gonzalez Aguirre
reviews.text:
A Substandard Experience at Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa (by Meliá)

We recently stayed at Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa (by Meliá) expecting a high-end brand, but unfortunately, the experience fell far short of expectations. From day one, the food was poor: dinner at the Japanese restaurant was unacceptably bad, and several members of our group suffered from stomach upset and diarrhea the following day. Overall, the à la carte restaurants offered neither adequate quality nor superior to the buffet, which is unbecoming of a five-star hotel.

The snack bar service was equally subpar: we waited over an hour for a hamburger and two sandwiches, which, when they arrived, were not what we had ordered. The hamburger was burnt, and the sandwiches didn't match our order. When we reported the problem, we received no explanation or proposed solutions, and to top it all off, we were met with jokes and laughter from the staff. The treatment we received as customers was unacceptable.

In addition, the gym's air conditioning was inadequate throughout our stay. Despite repeatedly requesting an adjustment to the temperature and airflow, our requests were ignored, making it very uncomfortable to work out and causing one of us to develop a sore throat.

The room service also fell short of expectations. Cleaning was insufficient, and one day, at 6:00 PM, our room still hadn't been cleaned, forcing us to go down to reception. The worst experience was the laundry service: it took a day and a half to collect our clothes despite our reminders, and when they returned them, they were only ironed, with the previous stains still visible. Overall, an experience clearly below what one would expect from a five-star establishment.

We are publishing this review to reflect what happened and with the hope that improvements will be made. We await contact from the hotel chain to offer explanations and ensure that situations like this do not happen again.

reviews.author: Ana M
reviews.text:
We stayed at this hotel between November and December 2024. Enjoying our honeymoon, we booked one of the Master Suite Swim-Up rooms.

The hotel is quiet, clean, beautiful, and elegant, with facilities that exude comfort and make for a pleasant stay.

The service from the waiters was terrible: they only showed interest if they received a tip or dollars; otherwise, they practically ignored you and didn't bother to offer proper service. This attitude created a feeling of complete disinterest and left much to be desired in terms of professionalism.

The most disappointing thing for us was the service we received in the Chinese show cooking area. The chef, Rafa, was particularly unpleasant with my husband, displaying a rude and even discourteous attitude. This behavior created an uncomfortable situation that completely marred our experience.

In contrast, we want to highlight Salvador, the young man in charge of excursions. He was very kind and helpful at all times.

This demonstrates his professionalism and positive attitude towards guests.

And to add to that, the steakhouse was a definite plus, where the waiters were exemplary and the meat was delicious.

In contrast, the Italian restaurant left much to be desired.

This hotel desperately needs more oversight. It gives the impression that management is either unaware of what's going on or, worse, that they prefer to turn a blind eye. When you spend such a large sum of money on a honeymoon, the least you expect is a good experience, not poor service and unprofessional attitudes. It's unacceptable that a place with such beautiful and tranquil facilities ends up failing due to poor management.

reviews.author: Paula Maldonado
reviews.text: The room was lovely. But the service was terrible. You have to ask for everything a thousand times, and even then they don't deliver. Basic things. In the restaurants, they turn off the air conditioning and take forever to bring the food—an hour and a half. The staff are unhelpful, with bad attitudes and a negative vibe.

reviews.author: Francis Salce Nuñez
reviews.text:
My experience at the Paradisus Palma Real & Golf hotel fell far short of expectations for its category and price. The service was poor, with little customer service and a lack of follow-up on problems reported during my stay. The facilities, while seemingly luxurious, were not in the best condition, which caused discomfort. The value for money is very low, as what is offered does not meet the advertised standard.

I definitely would not recommend this hotel and believe there are options in the area with much better service and professionalism.

reviews.author: MR.Elyon.
reviews.text:
A Huge Disappointment at the Paradisus Palma Real – Unacceptable Management

We stayed for 10 days at the Paradisus Palma Real hotel in Punta Cana, a trip we were eagerly anticipating, but which unfortunately turned into a huge disappointment due to the poor management and lack of professionalism of some of the staff, especially the person in charge of restaurant reservations and ensuring the well-being and comfort of guests: a man named Gilbert.

Gilbert was, without a doubt, a complete fraud. Throughout our entire stay, he showed absolutely no interest in helping us. He didn't manage our reservations correctly, he didn't answer our questions, and he didn't care about our comfort. He simply ignored us. For a hotel that prides itself on luxury and high-level service, it is unacceptable to have such an incompetent employee in a key position.

In contrast, we want to highlight the excellent service we received at the beach bar. There, Pedro was an exemplary waiter, with a professional, friendly, and approachable manner—someone who clearly has years of dedicated experience. Marcos Ignacio, another waiter, also deserves a special mention: a true professional, always polite and attentive. They were undoubtedly the best thing about the hotel.

The rooms were fine, comfortable, and clean, although the food, frankly, could be much better, especially considering the hotel's level and price.

Another major problem was the "Reserve" service. We paid a significant supplement because there were six of us and we wanted to enjoy this supposedly premium experience. However, we were unpleasantly surprised to find that the "Reserve" area was closed to the public. We were charged for a service that wasn't available, and we weren't even offered a solution or compensation. We felt this was an abuse and a lack of respect for the customer.

In short, the hotel has potential, but the management is terrible in certain fundamental aspects. Gilbert was a complete disappointment, and charging us for the "Reserve" service without being able to use it was a blatant rip-off. Fortunately, staff like Pedro and Marcos Ignacio redeemed the experience, but for the price we paid, we expected much more.

Thank you, Pedro and Marco, for making our stay enjoyable!

reviews.author: Maria Cecilia Valdes
reviews.text: Poor food quality, especially in the main restaurant and outdoor area. The waiters were rude, and the grill cook was even worse. Everyone handling food grabbed it with their bare hands without using gloves or the proper utensils. My room wasn't cleaned several days during my 15-day stay. In general, cleaning under the bed was practically nonexistent. Naturally, I won't be returning because my stay wasn't free. I must also acknowledge that some of the cooks at the breakfast buffet were very friendly.

reviews.author: Daniel Bautista Lopez
reviews.text:
The service was terrible. Only the reception staff and bartenders treated me well. The food was nowhere near what I expected for spending $571 for one night. I must say the room was very comfortable, but I would have preferred to sleep on hot asphalt at noon as long as I was treated well and had good quality, tasty food. I ordered room service—what a mistake! The man who answered the phone treated me like I was his hostage, and I'm begging him for a little food after a month of being held captive. In short, I doubt there's anyone in charge of quality at that resort, but if there is, I'd completely rethink the operation of this all-inclusive. And if an investor reads this, I would recommend they withdraw all their assets from this hotel—fast! It's a ticking time bomb.

Daniel López - stayed in room 3314 from July 12-13, 2025

reviews.author: Shirley Pérez
reviews.text: The hotel itself was fine, but the service was terrible! From the waiters to the room service (who never answered), it was awful. Making reservations at the themed restaurants was impossible! A disaster. There are better hotels for the same price; save yourself the trip. They couldn't even clean the room. Everything was bad. The facilities were fine, but the service ruined everything else.

reviews.author: Jimmy Ciprian
reviews.text:
We stayed 3 nights at this hotel for a medical conference.

Without a doubt, this hotel urgently needs renovation in several areas:
1. The infrastructure is old and worn.

2. HYGIENE: This is a crucial point, and this hotel is sorely lacking in hygiene. The rooms are very dusty and full of mites. In the buffet restaurant, the heat and poor organization of all the food—cheeses and cold cuts that were clearly not kept refrigerated—are unbelievable. (Several attendees experienced gastrointestinal issues.)
3. SERVICE: If you're looking for service, this is definitely not the place. With the exception of Anthony at the lobby bar and Eduardo from guest services, everyone else was grumpy and tried to make your stay difficult.

4. FOOD: Generally of VERY poor quality.

reviews.author: cesar zayas
reviews.text:
⭐ 1 star
📍 Paradisus Royal Club Golf Resort – Punta Cana

A disastrous experience.
We received the worst service we've ever had at a hotel, especially as a family with children celebrating a birthday. From 6:00 pm until midnight, we were left without a room, despite having a full reservation. No one helped us, no one offered any solutions. The staff was indifferent, rude, and completely unprofessional.

The rooms they finally offered were dirty, smelled bad, and were completely neglected. The food was cold and of poor quality, and the service in the restaurants was slow and disorganized.

Furthermore, the hotel is not safe for families. We saw suspicious people, inappropriate behavior, and even what appeared to be drug sales within the hotel. It's unbelievable that this happens in a place that claims to be 5 stars.

There is no peace and quiet, no attentive service, no quality. All there is is terrible management and an unpleasant atmosphere. We feel completely cheated. This is not a 5-star hotel—it barely reaches 2.5 stars.

👉 I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. We'll never return.

reviews.author: Hernan Cortes
reviews.text: I absolutely do not recommend this place. The food and service are of the lowest possible quality. The rooms are okay, but it's extremely expensive to pay what they charge just for a decent room. Otherwise, both the food and service leave much to be desired.

reviews.author: MARIANO G.
reviews.text: The hotel is good. The bar service is bad. They call it all-inclusive, but it's a buffet with gaps of more than two hours where no food is available. And it's all junk food. If you don't eat fried food or drink alcohol, you won't get a single piece of fruit or yogurt between 3 and 6 pm. They only offer junk food for afternoon tea. The bar staff, with a few exceptions, are a disaster; they don't look at you, they mutter under their breath, and they get annoyed when you make a drink. Honestly, it felt like a rip-off during this vacation. It's nothing like the Grand Palladium. Even Los Pinos in Termas de Río Hondo, Argentina, offers better food and drinks.

reviews.author: dominique birkner
reviews.text:
Terrible service. We came here about 3 years ago, and the service, restaurants, and facilities were perfect.

This time, expectations were much lower: the facilities were poor, the service was terrible, and especially the staff. The only redeeming feature is how the food has improved.

Very different from 3 years ago. If you're not a tipper, they'll always treat you poorly. They'll turn a deaf ear and bring you anything.

In fact, they don't even have volleyballs, but they have 3 courts. Now everything is charged for: a gin? A beer? A tequila? You pay for everything!

reviews.author: Liezer Alcántara
reviews.text: The hotel is fine, small, compact and cozy, but the service is very poor and if you can't make a dinner reservation at a restaurant, you're literally better off taking the car and going out.

reviews.author: Maria Victoria Issa
reviews.text: The hotel is very nice, it's a shame the service is so terrible. Check-in was delayed by about 20 minutes because they wanted to charge us again for the room. The breakfast service is very slow. We asked for the capsules in our room to be replaced two days ago and nothing has been done. On top of that, it was 3 pm and they still hadn't cleaned our room. Most of the staff are unfriendly. I don't recommend it.

reviews.author: Roju Services Corporation
reviews.text:
I'm sorry to write this review, but I'm going to speak from experience.
First of all, this hotel is supposedly 5-star, but that doesn't seem to be true. I say this because this is my third time in Punta Cana, but the first time I've been to this hotel. They supposedly claim to be 5-star, but compared to others I've been to, this one leaves a lot to be desired. I stayed from Wednesday, September 4th to September 8th, 2024, in room 2112. The shower in this room was in poor condition; it flooded, and water spilled into the sink when I showered. I'll attach a photo.
The food: The buffets are small and don't have many options. The a la carte restaurants aren't very good either, especially the Asian, Italian, and Mexican restaurants. The steakhouse was a little better.
The service: It's very sad and frustrating that you only get good service if you tip the staff. If you don't, they give you dirty looks and rude service. In short, there are better options in Punta Cana at 5-star hotels; I honestly don't recommend this one at all.

reviews.author: lorena setien alonso
reviews.text: A very poor experience for what we paid. And that's despite the hotel being at very low occupancy! The room was cobwebs and uncleaned, the minibar wasn't restocked even though we arrived late at night. The butler service left much to be desired (specifically my butler; the rest were quite helpful). The restaurant staff were lovely. The themed restaurants were acceptable; the best were Mina and The Winery. The Reserve is not worth the extra cost. In my case, it was awful. The resort is very beautiful and welcoming, but not worth the price.

reviews.author: Daniel lee
reviews.text:
Here, Otium Tour scammed us.

Don't let them ruin your trip like they did ours.

It's the Otium travel agency, located on the first floor of the Paradisus Hotel.

(A total of 5 people filed complaints).

Explanation: We had clearly made a reservation, but they told us it wasn't registered. Even when we showed them the booking confirmation, they claimed the information was incorrect. We finally managed to prove our reservation, but then they suddenly told us the tour was canceled and we couldn't go. They also pressured us to book a more expensive tour.

They take no responsibility whatsoever.
If you can, book your trip with an agency that guarantees confirmation of its services.

reviews.author: Juan Palacios Ituarte
reviews.text:
I've been trying to get an invoice for my stay for over two months, but there's no way. Every time I contact them, they offer kind words (phone or email), but no one does their job. This is in line with the hotel's terrible front desk service.
Otherwise, the rooms are very good, perhaps overly large, everything is well maintained, but the buffet food is quite poor and the theme restaurants are very limited... I expected more for the price of the accommodation. I wouldn't recommend it.
Edit: 1 day after posting the negative review: Apparently, Google stars are the only way to get a hotel to react. Less than two hours after posting the review, I received a message from the hotel management apologizing for the service, and 5 minutes later I had the invoices... It's a joke that the only way to get a response is to give stars on Google.

reviews.author: Alessandro Arrighi
reviews.text: The hotel is certainly beautiful and the food is excellent. But the rooms, pompously labeled suites, are truly awful. My "suite" didn't even have a double bed. The bathrooms are connected to the rest of the room, and the filthiness spreads to the sleeping area. No upgrade for Circle Gold status. The food in the restaurants is fabulous compared to other all-inclusives I've been to. The front desk staff is unpleasant and unprofessional.

reviews.author: Luiz Felipe Carleto
reviews.text:
The worst experience I've ever had in hotels of this "level".

Terrible service, rude staff, each one says something different about the hotel's rules/operations. Extremely slow service, with food or drinks, to the point of giving up on the request. If you tip, you're treated better; without a tip, you become garbage.

Furthermore, several items from the all-inclusive package are always out of stock in some parts of the hotel. And the drinks, which should be cold, are always warm.

In short, I wouldn't go back even for free!

reviews.author: Tommy Batista Germoso
reviews.text: Restaurant reservations don't work, the service is rude, the Mediterranean restaurant even had a cockroach. Room service never arrived. The reservation and payment were for three people, but the room only had one bed. The food was cold in most places. The room was assigned to several guests at the same time. They refuse to accept or provide service.

reviews.author: Mónica Hoefken Raffo
reviews.text:
The security department was inadequate. We lost a cell phone and they didn't give us an explanation, nor did they review the security camera footage despite knowing the exact date, time, and location where it was lost.

As for the activities, the entertainment team and Jorge Rafael provided excellent service.
Lucía and her team also provided excellent service at the main bar.
The food and wine quality need improvement.
The gym facilities and service were very good.
Our concierge, Rosemarie, was attentive to our needs.

reviews.author: bruno josé herrera ramírez
reviews.text: Terrible customer service, just one problem after another with no timely solutions. They misassigned reservations (we were given only one bed for three adults), then had problems with the door with over an hour's wait for assistance. A terrible experience.

reviews.author: Juliana Bereta
reviews.text:
The only thing that deserves the stars is the pool bar staff, Luis, Victor, and the waiters who go out of their way for you.
The food leaves much to be desired. Breakfast lacks fruit like bananas or apples, for example; you have to beg for even such basic fruit.
The buffet is awful, very poorly cooked. Pasta, for instance, is either overcooked or very hard, and the sauces are inedible. The buffet has eggplant prepared in every way imaginable: roasted, stewed, fried, in salads, etc. The oil for dressing is sunflower oil; there's no virgin olive oil. Chicken isn't available, and they tell you they're out. There's no beef steak either. The buffet basically consists of pork meatballs, pork stew, and a supermarket hamburger—very cheap, don't even think about a homemade burger. Boiled corn on the cob is served every day, even in milk, along with stewed cabbage and stewed carrots. I've never been to such a bad and expensive buffet.

I've been a customer for 15 years, and the decline is noticeable. There are no more snacks at the pool bar; they don't even have Fanta, for example, yet you pay a lot of euros a day for an all-inclusive package. There was no shower gel in the room, and it took us three days to get some. There wasn't even any soap to wash our hands. They really need to review how they're treating their guests. The included restaurants are all full, and even though you're entitled to a table, they won't serve you. We asked our butler, and she did what she could. But the price isn't low; the hotel is extremely expensive.

reviews.author: Sarah Maria
reviews.text:
We are a group of eight at the Paradisus Hotel.

The food is a complete disaster.

Cold and tasteless.

We booked an upgrade and paid over €1000 per room for better amenities.

What was promised to us was not delivered.

The room wasn't cleaned. Used underwear was found in one of the three rooms we booked. It was a horrible experience.

We are on vacation with a small baby, and this is an absolute catastrophe.

We then tried to resolve the issue with the manager, and

the room was cleaned.

But the next day, it was the same again; it wasn't clean. You can't eat at any of the à la carte restaurants because they are supposedly fully booked, even though you paid for the upgrade.

This means eating at the buffet restaurant for 12 days straight—that's unacceptable.

The staff is very unfriendly, even though we tip generously.

This is absolutely unacceptable.

I am very disappointed.

We don't know what to do next. 🥺

reviews.author: Patricia Lahera
reviews.text:
We chose this hotel for a vacation with friends and family (13 in total), all with babies under one year old. We clearly needed a good vacation :). I've been to other Paradisus hotels and was in love with this hotel chain. Sadly, the service, food, and room left much to be desired, as the experience was very bad.
First of all, the service is extremely poor. Interestingly, although the staff try to be kind and friendly, the disorganization, lack of training (no one knows what time their restaurants open and close, and they made us walk from one place to another without success), and the quality of the food make it impossible to provide quality service.
The food... the buffet at the NAOS restaurant is good, but the specialty restaurants are very poor... We waited two hours for our order to be taken, another hour for our food, and three hours for dinner. They made a mistake with the order and brought everything at different times. Sadly, a disaster, because other Paradisus hotels seem excellent to me.
On the other hand, it's almost impossible to get reservations at the restaurants, even when they're almost empty and the hotel is at 40% occupancy...
The room: We suffered from a leak all night because the upstairs neighbor was using the jacuzzi. Honestly, it was annoying, but maintenance responded quickly, and although we decided not to change rooms because we have a baby who's a few months old (already asleep), they offered to change our room.
I hope these comments help them improve these details because the facilities are nice, rustic (they need an update), the rooms are very spacious, with a jacuzzi, and the common areas are very nice, but overall our experience has been poor. We still have 3 days left; I'll update if anything changes.
Thanks!

reviews.author: Монастырская Анна
reviews.text:
Terrible hotel. The rooms are old, run-down, and dirty. We were put in a room where the doors didn't close, there were broken wardrobes and a toilet.
The rooms are poorly cleaned, and the bed was changed only once in two weeks.
Terrible service, nothing more. Unpleasant staff.
More than 50% of the staff don't speak English.
The food is also terrible: vegetables, main dishes are impossible to eat, and there's no taste.
There's no relaxation room in the spa, nothing. In the massage rooms, the dirty floor lies unpleasantly on the couch. This was the most expensive and worst massage ever. I paid $210 for 1 hour and 20 minutes!!!

I've never been in a worse hotel in my life, never come here.

Terrible hotel. The rooms are old, falling apart, and dirty. We were put in a room where the doors didn't close, and the closets and toilet were broken.
The rooms are poorly cleaned; the bed linen was changed only once in two weeks. Terrible service, or rather, nonexistent. Unpleasant staff.
More than 50% of the staff don't speak English.
The food is also terrible: the vegetables and main courses are edible, tasteless.
The spa has no relaxation room or anything. The massage rooms have dirty floors, making it uncomfortable to lie down on the massage table. This was the most expensive and worst massage I've ever had. I paid $210 for 1 hour and 20 minutes!!!

I've never been to a more terrible hotel in my life. Never come here.

reviews.author: Lazaro Puertas
reviews.text: Terrible experience with OTIUM. If I could give them less than one star, I would. We waited for over an hour for transportation and it never showed up. The worst of the worst. The whole family woke up early and didn't even have breakfast. They have no sense of responsibility. Salvador helped us, and the transportation company was Bávaro Runners.

reviews.author: Ignacio Cardenas Lares
reviews.text: It's nearly impossible to make a reservation at a restaurant, even though the hotel is never at 50% occupancy. There's a lot of disorganization, and you can ask two different hotel employees the same question and get different answers. Although the "Reserve" category includes access to premium liquors, they practically never have them. The concierge is very confusing and not very clear with information. Some friends of mine almost had their luggage lost. The food portions are very small at the à la carte restaurants.

reviews.author: Ricardo Asin
reviews.text:
Hello, good afternoon. I wanted to share some feedback about my vacation from July 28th to August 5th at the Paradisus Palma Real Hotel in the Dominican Republic. My wife, my two 20-year-old children, and I stayed at the hotel, occupying two rooms. We shared two rooms with a friend and their daughters.
We were very warmly welcomed at the hotel, courtesy of the travel agent who works with you. The couples were given "superior rooms," which we settled into. Upon arrival, we noticed that the rooms were outdated and didn't qualify as suites. We were later informed by other guests that this area of ​​the hotel was old and hadn't yet been renovated. Subsequently, our rooms were changed to similar rooms to my children's, the only difference being that our rooms had twin beds, while my children's rooms had a double bed. I went to reception and requested a double bed for myself and that my children's beds be separated. They told me they would take care of my room, which they did, but they never changed my children's room. I went back to reception to reiterate my request, and they very cheerfully told me that I should have switched rooms with my children, and they never addressed my complaint again.

Regarding the hotel restaurant, I must say that the food was good and varied, but certain dishes (seafood) and desserts were scarce. The staff only paid attention when we were seated at the table, and then they never bothered to even bring us a glass of water. The dining room was as low-class as the hotel's category: no tablecloths, no air conditioning, very small, and, I repeat, the staff's service was unreliable. As for the beach service, the four entertainers only offered brief activities aimed solely at adults; there were no activities for teenagers or children. The buffet service was very limited; all they served all day, every day, was sausages and hamburgers, and there were no waiters circulating among the beach umbrellas offering service. When we wanted to use the spa, we learned that we had to pay for it, as well as for room service. For afternoon tea, there was nowhere to go except the beachside hamburgers and sausages. They did, however, bother us with one thing: calling our room every day at 9:00 a.m. to invite us to sales presentations for their timeshare system—that was the main objective of this hotel chain.

I traveled to Cancun and Playa del Carmen through your service and stayed at Iberostar hotels. My family, the couple we traveled with, and Iberostar were all extremely satisfied and highly recommend them to our friends and acquaintances. In fact, I will continue to stay with Iberostar on my future trips. I have no intention of ever returning to the Meliá chain, nor would I recommend it to anyone I know. Unfortunately, this experience helped me compare and avoid wasting my considerable money on options that fall far short of what I already know.

Regards and thanks, Ricardo Asin, ID 14774031

reviews.author: Carlos Martinez
reviews.text: A disaster. I'm here right now waiting to be assigned a room. I've never seen such disorganization. It's the worst resort I've ever stayed at. No one in charge is taking responsibility.

reviews.author: Ale Houston
reviews.text:
The worst all-inclusive resort in the Caribbean.

Getting a table at one of their restaurants is harder than being born in Syria. They have extremely restrictive reservation hours, and the system doesn't work. We made reservations for the entire week, and the "system" didn't register a single one. No one takes responsibility for the problems. There's a constant shortage of items on the menus. Even if there are tables available at the restaurants, they won't serve you if you don't have a reservation.

The buffet food and drinks are okay, like something you'd find at a supermarket deli. If you're hoping for a decent meal, try to get a reservation at Sal, the steakhouse that serves excellent picanha.

The spa? It's a rip-off. The treatments are more expensive than at genuine 5-star hotels.

Generally, if you want access to any amenities you'd expect from a 5-star hotel, you have to pay extra.

The room (a Junior Suite) smelled musty, the bathroom sink was broken, there was no elevator to reach three floors, and the minibar had fewer drinks and snacks than a teenager's apartment.

The service was generally very poor, with a few exceptions. The staff was aggressive and discourteous, and they looked at you with a "tip" expression even for a glass of water.

I wouldn't recommend this hotel to an enemy. Meliá should be ashamed of charging these rates for a run-down hotel managed by people who probably ran summer camps, not "5-star" hotels.

reviews.author: Jose Fdez Celeiro
reviews.text: The best part was Yaideli's attention. From then on, it was a disappointment. They practically forced us to buy a Circle by Melia membership, which is a scam! Don't fall for it! They're useless, and you end up signing up without even realizing it, committing to a 30-year contract with no way to cancel! The salespeople, especially Annerys Sánchez, are incredibly persistent and seem like a nice, humble guy, but like Juan Luis Espinola, they convince you to sign up with an expensive membership that offers no real benefits! It's useless! The service is terrible; they only want tips all the time. They even hide Presidente beer if you don't tip them! Look up Circle by Melia on TripAdvisor to see that I'm not the only one saying this and who has been scammed by these people. Search for comments about this on the Circle by Melia hotel page.

reviews.author: Carmen Chiaravalloti
reviews.text: It's a shame they've lowered the quality of all the services. This is the fourth time I've stayed at Meliá Level hotels and my first at Paradisus. From reception to accessing any service, it's been a real disappointment. Poor service, poor food quality in the restaurants and buffet. The supposedly luxurious apartment is far from it. The stars are an exaggeration. The good thing is that with these beaches, you don't even want to go near the hotel.

reviews.author: Jenny Ferreiras
reviews.text: The service in general is poor. It's a very large hotel with so few restaurants. Some areas look neglected. One night they didn't clean my room... The minibar is pathetic... In short, they charge a fortune and the service isn't luxurious... although I have to admit the food has improved considerably. It's good compared to a few years ago.

reviews.author: Nora Filizzola
reviews.text:
We are staying in room 3026 (suite with jacuzzi). Upon arrival, they didn't have a crib ready for our 20-month-old baby and told us there were no cribs available, despite having properly reserved the room. Their solution was for the baby to sleep without a crib until, finally, after much insistence, the crib arrived. The service at reception was terrible. Not even a day had passed before all the bathroom drains were clogged. These things can happen anywhere, but after several blockages, we requested a room change from the reception supervisor, Mr. José, and have been waiting since yesterday, despite reminding him again this morning. The facilities are good, but the service is poor; it's nothing like a 5-star hotel. Beautiful packaging for poor contents.

We will continue waiting for the room change.

reviews.author: Belén Garrido
reviews.text:
I made a reservation in September with The Reserve. It turns out they changed their name, and when I arrived at Palma Real, they told me I had to go to the Garden Suites. It's inferior to what I expected, and they didn't give me a clear explanation, even though I confirmed by phone many times in December that it was the same.
They couldn't seat me in the Palma Real; they put me somewhere else, but I spent an hour and a half arguing because they wouldn't give me any benefits, even though I was with a 3-year-old and tired from the flight.
The treatment was awful. The lack of information was appalling. Obviously, I knew absolutely nothing about the name change and all that; I had no reason to know. My vacation started off on the wrong foot, and no one offered me a concrete solution. It's a shame. Don't come here.

I'm editing because they replied that everyone was informed about the name change, but no, I haven't received any information at all. Furthermore, I contacted them personally in December, and no one told me anything. The reservations center said everything is the same. So, well, they continue down the path of lies and fraud.

reviews.author: Heronides Vasconcelos
reviews.text: For a hotel of this size and part of the Meliá chain, it leaves much to be desired, very much so. The experience was terrible right from check-in, where simple things like showing the room location weren't done. And to make matters worse, the key didn't work, even after going to reception twice to replace it. When I asked to speak to the manager, I was told he wasn't there.

reviews.author: Eliana Jara
reviews.text: The good: The private beach in front of the hotel... wonderful, the bad: the food... lousy and repeated and the undrinkable drinks. They sell a black bracelet to access the premium drinks that are only less bad... We went out to eat out and drink Caipirinhas for 200 exquisite Dominican pesos

reviews.author: Fertik
reviews.text:
I stayed there a few years ago and it was dreadful. If you're lucky enough to have everything go smoothly, perfect. But as soon as you have a problem, forget about it because they don't have complaint forms, and they won't accept any written complaints. It's truly third-world. I had a minor fall in my room because the floor was flooded, and they absolutely refused to let me file a complaint. Their only obsession was taking me on a pilgrimage to several fly-infested medical offices, which resulted in me losing the last day of my stay. But as for accepting complaints, absolutely nothing, and the person responsible was the manager, who was also Spanish.

If you want to take a chance, go to that hotel; you might get lucky. But at the slightest complication, you can pray to God and the Virgin Mary, you're doomed.

Please do not reply to this message; it is a review for the public, not the hotel.

They charged me for the reservation twice, and now I'm trying to check out early, but they want to charge me for the full amount. It's appalling.

reviews.text: There are Dominicans who are willing to pay for premium service, and it wasn't offered to us at check-in. I didn't like it because they seem more focused on foreigners than on Dominicans themselves. Very disappointed; this is the first and last time I'll visit Meliá hotels.

reviews.author: Isabella De La Pena
reviews.text: Eleven of us went on vacation and it was a complete ordeal. The worst customer service I've ever experienced. The hotel was incredibly boring; they didn't play music, there were no attractions, and the buffet always offered the same thing. When I arrived at my room on the first day, the refrigerator wasn't working, the bathroom was filthy, and there were no towels or bedspreads. I called to resolve the issue, but no one ever came to my room, and the same thing happened with the four rooms we rented. Then they moved us to different rooms, and the same problems occurred. The hotel fountains that are supposed to beautify the surroundings were broken. The hotel is completely neglected. We know the pandemic is affecting tourism in Punta Cana, especially hotels, but there are very basic things that are clearly neglected. With the money they're making, this hotel should at least have the basics. Currently, it's a two-star hotel (totally disappointed).

reviews.author: Josep Lluís Monasterio
reviews.text: The facilities and food are excellent, but the reception staff has the worst service imaginable. Their greed for selling services, surpassed only by their ineptitude, makes for a truly problematic stay. They forget requests, make calls at night to sell paintings, deprogram room key cards, and so on. The cleaning and entertainment services are highly questionable. I haven't seen anything like it in 50 years and on four continents.

Let me tell you... after visiting Palma Real Punta Cana about two years ago, I fell in love with it, and now I'm the most disappointed guest. I've concluded that such a beautiful place with such a modern structure shouldn't be used to its full potential. As a customer, I'm completely overwhelmed and disappointed with this new "management."

reviews.text: I really didn't recommend this experience to anyone. The service is terrible; the employees are only interested in foreigners. There's no entertainment, it's very boring. I asked for my receipt with proof of payment, they were supposed to send it to my email, and I'm still waiting. I went to make a dinner reservation, and the young woman told me there were no reservations available. She said I had to pay $80, but she assumed I didn't have the money, and told me there were no reservations for that day. About 10 minutes later, my husband, who is white, arrived, and they did make a reservation for him. It's disappointing.

reviews.author: Iñigo Goñi
reviews.text:
Our experience at this hotel was truly disappointing, especially regarding the check-in service. The process was extremely slow, disorganized, and unprofessional. We had the constant feeling that the staff were neither well-prepared nor knew how to handle the situation, which resulted in a long and unnecessary wait.

We are regular guests of the Meliá chain and are familiar with the level of quality they typically offer across their various brands, so this experience surprised us even more, and not in a good way. It's regrettable that something as basic as check-in becomes such a major problem. A simple inconvenience ends up turning into an interminable wait and a build-up of frustrations.

We hope that you will take steps to improve this aspect, as it directly affects the guest's first impression and falls far short of what one expects from this hotel group.
